signals.review_reason: 三个 issue 均描述同一根因：子进程 stderr/异常结构信息在传播链中被丢弃或隐藏，导致用户面对无意义的泛化错误无法诊断和恢复。Issue #913 有两次独立复现，均在主流程（CI 等待阶段）阻断且产生真实成本；Issue #800 和 #810 进一步证明这是系统性设计缺陷而非偶发问题。高频+主流程阻断+明确成本损失+反复失败，P0 定义完全满足。

source_issues.title: SDK subprocess crash during long-running queries with heavy MCP polling — stderr swallowed, error message uninformative
source_issues.evidence: 两个独立会话在完全相同的 61 轮次精确崩溃，堆栈一致，stderr 被吞没，错误信息为 'Check stderr output for details' 但实际未暴露 stderr 内容，阻断主流程（wait-for-pipeline 阶段 CI 等待失败），已产生实际成本（$1.62 和 $1.63）

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded 'Check stderr output for details' placeholder
source_issues.evidence: 原始 ProcessError 的 exit_code 和 stderr 在传播中被摧毁，三处缺陷：(1) stderr 被硬编码占位符替代 (2) query.py 将异常降级为 str 丢失所有结构 (3) receive_messages 重新抛出裸 Exception，用户无法捕获原始异常获取诊断信息

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: anyio task group 与 cancel scope 跨任务退出导致 CPU 持续 100% 占用（pinned CPU），同一模式在 #454 和 #776 中出现过，#746 的修复不完整，说明是反复出现的已知问题

signals.topic: 异步传输层异常处理和资源泄漏导致生产环境不可靠
signals.summary: BaseExceptionGroup 逃脱 close()、anyio MemoryObjectStream 未关闭、task group cancel scope 泄漏——三类异步资源泄漏均未被正确清理，导致生产环境中出现 CPU 满载、内存泄漏和异常逃逸。
aliases: MemoryObjectStream not closed on query completion
signals.review_reason: 三个 issue 均指向异步传输层的资源清理缺陷：(1) CancelledError 逃逸损坏事件循环 (2) MemoryObjectStream 内存泄漏 (3) task group cancel scope 导致 CPU 满载。这些缺陷在生产环境中会导致资源持续泄漏和运行时不稳定，虽然非单次阻断但影响系统长期可靠性，P1。

source_issues.title: BaseExceptionGroup escapes transport.close() on second query() in the same event loop
source_issues.evidence: Python 3.11+ CancelledError 继承自 BaseException，suppress(Exception) 无法拦截 BaseExceptionGroup[CancelledError]，第二次 query() 时异常逃逸导致事件循环状态损坏，是生产环境中的稳定复现场景

source_issues.title: Resource Leak: anyio memory object stream associated with a query is leaked
source_issues.evidence: Query.close() 未对 self._message_send 和 self._message_receive 调用 aclose()，导致 anyio MemoryObjectStream 泄漏，在 PYTHONDEVMODE=1 下触发 ResourceWarning，可通过 PYTHONDEVMODE=1 稳定复现

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leak — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: anyio task group 与 cancel scope 跨任务退出导致 CPU pinned 100%，同类 bug 已在 #454 和 #776 出现两次，#746 的修复不完整，说明是系统性异步传输层问题

signals.topic: Windows 平台 MCP 服务器工具注册静默失败
signals.summary: 在 Windows 11 + Python 3.14 上，MCP 服务器配置对 agent 可见但工具实际返回 'No such tool available'，SDK 的 stdio-mode MCP 注入路径在 Windows 上静默失败。
aliases: MCP server tools fail on Windows
Win32 error when spawning Claude CLI
signals.review_reason: 两个 issue 均描述 Windows 上的 MCP/CLI 启动失败，Issue #902 有明确回归证据（前一天正常）、明确阻断场景（MCP 工具不可用）和平台覆盖（Windows 是主流平台），关键功能不可用，P1。Issue #901 是同一平台的独立表现形式。

source_issues.title: MCP server tools fail to register on Windows: server config visible to agent but tools return 'No such tool available'
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 + Python 3.14 上 MCP 服务器指令出现在 agent 上下文中但工具返回 'No such tool available'，SDK 的 stdio-mode MCP 注入路径在 Windows 上静默失败（未抛出异常），前一天（2026-04-30）还正常工作，是明显的回归问题，直接阻断 MCP 工具集成这一核心功能

source_issues.title: Tolaria and Claude Code (Win32 error)
source_issues.evidence: Win32 错误 '%1 ist keine zulässige Win32-Anwendung. (os error 193)' 导致 Claude Code 无法启动，属于主流程阻断性错误

signals.topic: fork_session() 非原子写入可导致会话数据损坏
signals.summary: fork_session() 使用 os.write() 而非 tmp+rename 原子模式，进程在写入中途崩溃会产生残缺的 .jsonl 文件，导致后续 list_sessions() 和会话恢复失败。
signals.review_reason: 单 issue，但数据完整性风险明确：非原子写入在进程崩溃场景下产生残缺会话文件，且 list_sessions() 对残缺文件的处理本身也有 bug（#904），两者叠加会导致用户丢失会话数据且无感知。P2 因 count=1 且为边缘场景。

source_issues.title: fork_session() write is non-atomic; crash mid-write leaves orphan transcript
source_issues.evidence: fork_session() 使用 os.open+os.write+os.close 无原子性保证，崩溃发生在 os.open 和 os.close 之间会产生残缺 .jsonl 文件，list_sessions() 的 _parse_session_lite() 对残缺文件解析行为未定义，可能返回 created_at=None 或解析失败，导致会话元数据丢失且用户无感知

signals.topic: API-key 用户被锁定在 5 分钟缓存 TTL（成本损失）
signals.summary: SDK v0.1.59 捆绑的 CLI 版本（2.1.105）早于 ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H 功能引入版本（2.1.108），导致 API-key 用户无法使用 1 小时 prompt cache TTL，在生产环境中持续以更高成本计费。
aliases: API-key users stuck on 5m cache TTL
prompt caching 1h TTL not available for API-key users
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但这是明确的成本损失场景：8 个月的持续过度计费，单客户估算 $11K/14 天有优化空间，且官方文档给出误导性表述（'automatic' savings）。P2 因影响范围有限但用户财务损失实质。

source_issues.title: API-key users silently stuck on 5m cache TTL: bundled CLI in v0.1.59 predates ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H opt-in
source_issues.evidence: 用户在生产环境运行了 8 个月后才发现自己所有 cache 写入都按 5 分钟层级计费而非 1 小时 TTL，官方文档声称 prompt caching savings 是 'automatic' 但实际对 API-key 用户不自动生效。客户估算 Sonnet agentic 支出 ~$11K/14 天有显著优化空间，这是明确且持续的成本损失。

signals.topic: SDK sets excessive cache breakpoints on null-content turns causing significant per-turn cost inflation
signals.summary: The SDK reports ~65K cache_creation_input_tokens per turn even when content is byte-identical (null-content turns with stable system prompt + tools), causing $0.50-$0.65 per-turn cost on Opus. Users are paying full API price for no-value exchanges.
signals.review_reason: Significant cost loss ($0.50-$0.65 per null-content turn) caused by SDK setting cache breakpoints redundantly. Affects all users with multi-turn sessions. Clear quantitative evidence in issue body.

source_issues.title: cache issues in sdk
source_issues.evidence: SDK reports ~65K cache_creation_input_tokens per turn on null-content turns. Per-turn cost on Opus lands at $0.50-$0.65 even for trivial null-content exchanges, dominated by 65K cache_create. User explicitly documents cost impact data and raises question about SDK setting cache breakpoints at every turn.

signals.topic: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel sessions fail with TypeError before receiving any events
signals.summary: Firing multiple beta.sessions.events.stream() calls results in 4 out of 5 streams failing with TypeError before any events arrive. The standard Messages API works reliably with identical parameters, isolating the failure to the beta.sessions lifecycle.
signals.review_reason: 80% failure rate on beta.sessions stream API with consistent TypeError before any events. Key beta feature (sessions) is effectively broken in parallel usage scenarios.

source_issues.title: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel (and serial) sessions fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events
source_issues.evidence: 4 of 5 beta.sessions.events.stream() calls fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events arrive. Reproducible consistently. Standard Messages API works reliably with identical auth/prompt/model parameters, confirming the bug is in beta.sessions lifecycle.

signals.topic: query() with json_schema outputFormat crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel')
signals.summary: Using outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema' } in a minimal query() call causes an internal SDK crash with a null reference error, preventing any structured output from being returned.
signals.review_reason: Deterministic SDK crash for a common structured output use case (json_schema). Users cannot use the json_schema output format at all. Clear blocking bug.

source_issues.title: query() with minimal outputFormat: { type: "json_schema" } can crash internally with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel')`
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic crash inside the SDK with TypeError before any assistant output or structured output is returned when using json_schema outputFormat. SDK crashes internally rather than returning a helpful error.

signals.topic: Subagents cannot access MCP server resources declared in their own agent definitions, blocking multi-agent architectures
signals.summary: MCP servers declared in a subagent's configuration are not accessible to that subagent, forcing users to declare all MCP servers in the parent/orchestrator agent. This breaks isolation and modularity of multi-agent systems.
signals.review_reason: Blocks multi-agent architecture pattern which is a core use case for the SDK. Forces anti-pattern of centralizing all MCP config in parent agent. While only 1 issue, the pattern represents a fundamental architectural limitation.

source_issues.title: Subagents cannot access MCP server resources declared in subagent definitions
source_issues.evidence: Subagents cannot invoke tools or read resources from their configured MCP servers. Workaround requires declaring all MCP servers in the parent orchestrator, eliminating subagent isolation. Affects multi-agent architecture patterns.

signals.topic: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude instead of resolving plugin-loaded agent names
signals.summary: The SDK's Options.agent parameter silently falls back to default Claude when given a plugin-loaded agent name, despite JSDoc claiming it is equivalent to the --agent CLI flag. Users cannot programmatically select plugin agents.
signals.review_reason: Silent behavior divergence from documented behavior. Users relying on the JSDoc contract get wrong agent silently. Degrades trust in SDK API reliability.

source_issues.title: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude for plugin-loaded agent names
source_issues.evidence: JSDoc on Options.agent states 'This is equivalent to the --agent CLI flag' but it does not resolve plugin agents while CLI does. Silent fallback means wrong agent is used without warning to user.

signals.topic: Self-hosted runners behind firewall fail after v1.0.100 due to install.sh masking curl failures and bypassing SDK bundled binary fallback
signals.summary: v1.0.100 introduced a regression where `install.sh` curl failures are silently ignored (bash pipe exits 0) and the SDK is given a non-existent binary path instead of falling back to its bundled platform binary. On self-hosted runners where claude.ai is unreachable (corporate firewall) but npm registry mirrors work, this causes the action to crash with 'native binary not found' instead of using the bundled SDK binary.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression that completely breaks the action in corporate self-hosted environments. The install.sh silently masks curl SSL failures and passes a non-existent binary path to the SDK, disabling the bundled binary fallback. The user provides clear before/after CI logs demonstrating the regression. Count=1 because it's a single reported incident, but impact is severe (blocks entire CI pipelines).

source_issues.title: v1.0.100 breaks environments where claude.ai is unreachable (install.sh silently fails, SDK bundled binary bypassed)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression from v1.0.100. CI logs show curl SSL error (35) followed by 'Claude Code installed successfully' and then 'ReferenceError: Claude Code native binary not found'. Same environment with v1.0.99 works via bundled binary fallback. Blocks entire deployment pipelines on self-hosted corporate runners.

signals.topic: Private/internal marketplace repositories fail to clone — git authentication not configured before plugin installation in base-action
signals.summary: When using `plugin_marketplaces` with a private or internal GitHub repository, the marketplace clone fails with 'repository not found' because `configureGitAuth()` is only called in agent/tag modes but marketplace installation happens in the base-action entry point before that. Users with proper GitHub App access to private repos cannot use them as plugin marketplaces without creating additional PATs.
signals.review_reason: Clear root cause with identified code location. Blocks the core use case of private/internal plugin marketplaces, forcing users to create additional PATs for a security-sensitive operation. The 'repository not found' error is misleading since the user has valid token access — it's a configuration ordering bug.

source_issues.title: Bug: Marketplace cloning fails with 'repository not found' for private/internal repos - git authentication not configured
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: `configureGitAuth()` is called in agent/tag modes but marketplace installation in `base-action/src/index.ts` → `installPlugins()` spawns `claude plugin marketplace add` without git credentials configured. 'Repository not found' is GitHub's standard error for permission denied. Blocks private marketplace adoption, forcing users to create additional PATs.

signals.topic: `.claude-pr/` snapshot directory is unintentionally committed to PR branches on fix-up commits
signals.summary: The `restoreConfigFromBase` snapshot directory `.claude-pr/` (created to preserve PR-context .claude/ and CLAUDE.md files) is committed to the user's PR branch whenever Claude bot makes a fix-up commit via `git add -A`. The existing `git reset` protection for SENSITIVE_PATHS is missing for `.claude-pr/` itself, causing stealth chore commits that the bot's reply comment doesn't acknowledge.
signals.review_reason: Pollutes users' PR commit history with unrelated ephemeral snapshot files, creating a confusing and unprofessional git history. The bot's silence about these commits means users don't know when it happened. The suggested fix is straightforward (add to `.git/info/exclude`), but the current behavior actively misleads maintainers about what changed.

source_issues.title: `restoreConfigFromBase` snapshot at `.claude-pr/` gets committed to PR branch when bot pushes a fix
source_issues.evidence: Two confirmed stealth commits in private org repo: (1) initial `.claude-pr/` (~100 files) committed on unrelated PR, (2) re-sync of `.claude-pr/` on another PR. Bot reply comment only mentions the requested fix, so maintainers only discover the extra commits on review. The `.claude-pr/` directory contains full `.claude/skills/` trees. On repeated `@claude` invocations, the now-tracked `.claude-pr/` causes repeated chore commits.

signals.topic: GitHub Copilot SWE agent actor 'Copilot' causes 404 crash in checkHumanActor before allowed_bots logic is consulted
signals.summary: When the GitHub Copilot SWE agent triggers the action, GitHub sets GITHUB_ACTOR to 'Copilot' (no [bot] suffix), but `GET /users/Copilot` returns 404 since there is no resolvable GitHub user under that login. The action crashes in `checkHumanActor` before reaching `allowed_bots`, so setting `allowed_bots: '*'` has no effect. The `allowed_non_write_users` bypass works for checkWritePermissions but not for the separate checkHumanActor call.
signals.review_reason: Completely blocks the integration of GitHub Copilot SWE agent with claude-code-action. The action crashes with exit code 1 before any meaningful work begins. The `allowed_bots` configuration is entirely bypassed due to the 404 crash ordering. This is a GitHub platform inconsistency (Copilot SWE agent doesn't use [bot] suffix) but the action must handle it gracefully.

source_issues.title: Action fails with "Not Found" when triggered by GitHub Copilot (actor Copilot returns 404 from/users/ API)
source_issues.evidence: CI logs show: 'Checking permissions for actor: Copilot', 'Warning: SECURITY WARNING: Bypassing write permission check for Copilot due to allowed_non_write_users', then 'GET /users/Copilot - 404 in 193ms', 'Error: Action failed with error: Not Found'. The action exits with code 1. `allowed_bots: '*'` is completely unreachable. This blocks the Copilot SWE agent + Claude Code Action integration entirely.

signals.topic: OAuth tokens stop working (validateHeaders crash) after Pro→Max subscription plan upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading from Pro to Max subscription, the action consistently fails with 'Could not resolve authentication credentials' from the SDK's validateHeaders check. The OAuth token is passed correctly (visible in logs), OIDC exchange succeeds, but the Claude Code subprocess receives both apiKey and authToken as null. The same token and workflow worked reliably before the plan upgrade. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` works as a workaround, but defeats the purpose of OAuth for subscription users.
aliases: Pro Max upgrade OAuth token broken
signals.review_reason: Affects users upgrading their Claude.ai subscription, which is an expected workflow that should not break. The action becomes completely non-functional via OAuth after a plan change, forcing users to switch to API key authentication. The provided CI logs show the full chain: token present → OIDC success → SDK receives null credentials → crash. The intermittent nature (one run worked mid-debugging) suggests a race condition with org context propagation.

source_issues.title: Intermittent `validateHeaders` failure with Max-plan OAuth tokens after Pro→Max upgrade
source_issues.evidence: User provides full CI logs showing OIDC token obtained, app token obtained, but SDK execution error: 'validateHeaders ... throw Error(Could not resolve authentication credentials)'. Token regenerated multiple times, format confirmed correct (sk-ant-oat01-...). 'claude auth status' shows correct Max subscription locally. Related to #1126 and #676. Intermittent: one run worked mid-debugging but next failed again — suggests a race condition or timing issue related to org context change.

signals.topic: False-positive filter uses deprecated Haiku model causing silent 404 failures on every run
signals.summary: The FP-filter step calls the deprecated 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' model, which returns 404 on every action run. This silently disables noise filtering, causing all raw findings to be posted as unfiltered PR comments.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine workflow degradation: the FP-filter is a core step in the security-review action, its failure is silent (no error thrown to fail the action), and the consequence is that all noise findings appear as unfiltered PR comments on every run. This directly impairs the action's value proposition and generates unnecessary CI noise. Count=1 (single issue in dataset), so P0 threshold not met, but the per-run impact justifies P1.

source_issues.title: False-positive filter fails with 404: model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' not found
source_issues.evidence: Action run returns 404 for 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' model every execution. Log shows '[claudecode.findings_filter] Claude API validation failed'. Main scan completes but FP filter is silently disabled — every raw finding is posted as a PR comment without noise filtering.

signals.topic: Ultrareview crashes consume free-tier quota credits without producing any findings
signals.summary: The /ultrareview command crashes on large PRs or due to server-side rate limits before producing any findings, but the free-tier quota counter still decrements. Users lose credits for runs that produced zero output, with no automatic refund mechanism.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report the same issue: ultrareview crashes (large PR size or server-side rate limit) consume free-tier credits with zero output delivered. This is a direct cost loss for users on the free tier. The count is exactly 2 based on deduplicated issues 56435 and 56432.

source_issues.title: /ultrareview crashed twice on large PR — consumed 2/3 free credits without producing findings
source_issues.evidence: 2 of 3 free ultrareview credits consumed on a large PR (69 commits, 221 files). Both runs returned 'Review crashed before producing findings' error. User requests credit restoration.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Free ultrareview quota consumed when run crashes before producing findings (server-side rate limit)
source_issues.evidence: Free ultrareview run crashed due to Anthropic-side rate limiting, returned error stub instead of findings. Quota counter went from '1 of 3' to '2 of 3' despite zero output delivered. User requests credit refund for the failed run.

signals.topic: Cowork sandbox disk accumulation causes session boot failure
signals.summary: The /sessions mount inside Cowork sandboxes does not garbage-collect old session directories, causing disk to fill to capacity (~90%) and new sessions to fail with 'useradd: No space left on device'. Users must quit and restart the app to recover, and the failure repeats every 2-3 months for active users. No warning is given before hitting the wall.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear user-blocking failure: active Cowork users cannot create new sessions when the /sessions mount fills up. The failure is reproducible (any user with sufficient session history will hit it), has a clear root cause (no GC of old session directories), and the user must perform a workaround (quit/restart app) to recover. Recurrence rate is predictable (~2-3 months).

source_issues.title: Cowork Session Disk Accumulation Errors
source_issues.evidence: Disk at 8.3G/9.8G (90%) with 195 leftover session directories dating back 2 months. New sessions fail with 'useradd: No space left on device; try again later'. App restart required. Problem repeats every ~2 months for active users.

signals.topic: API error: empty text blocks block message sending during follow-up requests
signals.summary: Claude Code sends API requests with 'cache_control cannot be set for empty text blocks' or 'text content blocks must be non-empty' errors, blocking users from continuing conversations with follow-up requests. Regression — worked in previous versions.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the primary workflow — users cannot send follow-up messages. This is explicitly marked as a regression (worked before v2.0.73+), confirming it is a new bug introduced by a recent change. Confirmed as blocking since users cannot proceed with their work.

source_issues.title: [BUG]
source_issues.evidence: User reports receiving 400 API errors 'messages.120.content.1.text: cache_control cannot be set for empty text blocks' and 'messages: text content blocks must be non-empty' when submitting follow-up requests. Error reproduced across multiple sessions. Is marked as a regression (worked in previous version).

signals.topic: Excessive/unexpected API token consumption during long Claude Code sessions
signals.summary: Users report dramatically inflated token usage — 49 seconds of a 'continue' action consumed 12% of a 5-hour rate limit window on Pro Max 5x plan. Associated with 'ensureToolResultPairing' errors repairing massive numbers of tool_result blocks, suggesting Claude Code is sending duplicate or redundant context to the API.
aliases: tool result pairing error inflated usage
signals.review_reason: Direct financial impact — a single 49-second action consuming 12% of a Pro Max 5x rate limit window represents significant cost to the user. The root cause appears to be a tool_result pairing issue causing redundant context to be sent to the API. Clear user impact evidence with specific numbers.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Excessive API token consumption during Claude Code sessions
source_issues.evidence: User reports 49-second 'continue' action consumed 12% of a 5-hour rate limit window on Pro Max 5x plan. Error log shows 'ensureToolResultPairing: repaired missing tool_result blocks' repairing hundreds of paired tool results, indicating excessive/redundant context being sent to API.

signals.topic: /mcp dialog ignores global ~/.claude/.mcp.json when project has no local .mcp.json
signals.summary: The /mcp dialog command only shows built-in MCP servers when run from a directory without a project-level .mcp.json, completely ignoring globally configured MCP servers. Meanwhile, 'claude mcp list' CLI command correctly shows all 8 globally configured servers. This makes the /mcp dialog unusable for users relying on global MCP configuration.
signals.review_reason: Core MCP feature is broken — the /mcp dialog (the primary UI for viewing MCP servers) silently ignores global configuration. While 'claude mcp list' works correctly, the dialog is the primary discovery mechanism. The discrepancy between the dialog showing 1 server vs CLI showing 8 is a clear functional gap. Has been reproduced by the user.

source_issues.title: Bug: /mcp dialog ignores global ~/.claude/.mcp.json when project has no .mcp.json
source_issues.evidence: User has 8 MCP servers configured globally in ~/.claude/.mcp.json. Running /mcp dialog from a directory without project-level config shows only 1 built-in server. 'claude mcp list' CLI correctly shows all 8 servers from the same directory. Issue is reproducible and confirmed as a bug in the /mcp dialog code path.

signals.topic: ralph-loop unbounded mode with no promise emitted — infinite loop with no safety net, wastes compute
signals.summary: When ralph-loop is started with max_iterations=0 (unbounded mode) and the model never emits the configured <promise> tag, the loop iterates indefinitely with no exit condition reachable without human intervention. A documented incident ran 6,239 iterations over ~11.7 hours, generating ~41,871 transcript messages. All three existing safeguards (SIGTERM, orphan watchdog, 2s hard exit) fail because the JS event loop is saturated. No no-op detection exists.
signals.review_reason: Significant cost loss plus workflow blocking: documented real-world incident wasted ~12 hours of compute with 6,239 iterations. The unbounded mode (max_iterations=0) with no promise emission creates a loop with zero reachable exit conditions — the most severe form of workflow failure. Two independent reports confirm the failure mode.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: add safety net for runaway when promise never emitted
source_issues.evidence: Real incident: 6,239 iterations over ~11.7 hours on 2026-05-03. State file confirmed max_iterations=0, empty session_id, promise never emitted. ~41,871 transcript messages. All three safeguards failed due to event loop saturation. Author provides no-op detection sketch, a working local fix (sleep 1.5), and hook-time trace evidence.

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: stop hook intermittently misses <promise> tag due to transcript flush race
source_issues.evidence: Hook-time trace evidence: pre-sleep size 262,679 bytes with no promise visible; post-sleep (1.5s) size 263,917 bytes with <promise>DONE</promise> visible (+1,238 bytes flushed inside race window). Direct observation of race in ralph-loop plugin. Same root cause as claude-code#15813 (closed not planned). 2 weeks of daily use with sleep 1.5 patch confirmed fix.

signals.topic: Windows incompatibility — SessionStart hook and LSP plugins fail to start on Windows
signals.summary: Two separate Windows compatibility failures: (1) SessionStart hook uses /usr/bin/bash which resolves to PE executable on Windows, causing 'cannot execute binary file' error at startup. (2) TypeScript LSP plugin hardcodes typescript-language-server command without extension; npm on Windows installs .cmd/.ps1 shims but no .exe, causing ENOENT on spawn. Both render respective features dead on arrival on Windows, a major platform.
signals.review_reason: Major platform (Windows) incompatibility that makes entire features fail. Both are reproducible and have clear root causes. Windows represents a significant portion of developers. One issue affects multiple plugins (typescript-lsp, potentially jdtls-lsp). Note: count=2 because there are two independent Windows failures (hook + LSP spawn), both verified by reporters.

source_issues.title: SessionStart hook fails on Windows: /usr/bin/bash is PE executable, not shell
source_issues.evidence: Error: /usr/bin/bash: /usr/bin/bash: cannot execute binary file. Git Bash on Windows resolves /usr/bin/bash to Git/bin/bash.exe which is PE32+, not a shell interpreter. Reproduction: enable plugin on Windows, start Claude Code, see error in startup output.

source_issues.title: typescript-lsp: ENOENT on Windows — libuv can't spawn typescript-language-server (.cmd shim, no .exe)
source_issues.evidence: /doctor reports: ENOENT no such file or directory, uv_spawn 'typescript-language-server'. npm installs typescript-language-server.cmd (not .exe) on Windows. uv_spawn requires explicit .cmd or shell:true. Plugin dead on arrival on Windows. Author notes jdtls-lsp likely has same issue.

signals.topic: code-review CWD inheritance failure in git worktrees — CLAUDE.md and git blame operate from wrong directory
signals.summary: When Claude Code runs in a git worktree, subagents spawned by the code-review plugin do not inherit the parent session's working directory. This causes CLAUDE.md file lookups to fail, git blame to operate from the wrong location, and code comments to target wrong files. Breaks multiple steps in the code-review pipeline.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure: code-review produces incorrect results in worktree setups (common developer pattern) because three of its key steps depend on file path context that subagents lose. CLAUDE.md discovery and git blame are core capabilities of the skill, not edge features.

source_issues.title: code-review: subagents don't receive CWD — CLAUDE.md lookup and git blame fail in worktree setups
source_issues.evidence: Step 2: Haiku agent cannot locate CLAUDE.md in worktree. Step 4c: Sonnet agent's git blame operates from wrong directory. Step 4e: code comment targets wrong files. Reproduced by user in worktree setup with 4-step repro.

signals.topic: iMessage parseAttributedBody truncates reply messages >127 UTF-8 bytes — content silently lost
signals.summary: The iMessage plugin's parseAttributedBody() misreads Apple typedstream length-prefix bytes, causing messages longer than ~127 UTF-8 bytes to be silently truncated at 64-255 bytes. This specifically affects messages sent via iOS 'Reply to specific message' feature whose text lives only in the attributedBody column. Users see incomplete messages with no indication of truncation.
signals.review_reason: Critical functionality unavailability: iMessage plugin loses actual message content for a specific but common message type. Users receive truncated text with no signal that content was lost. The bug is in a core message-parsing path, not an edge feature.

source_issues.title: iMessage: parseAttributedBody truncates reply-to messages >127 chars (typedstream length-prefix misread)
source_issues.evidence: User provided hex-level evidence from chat.db blob. Four reproducer messages decoded correctly with patch (820, 820, 383, 98 bytes) vs broken (64, 64, 131, 98). Real-world message truncated mid-word at 64th byte. Plugin version 0.1.0, macOS 25.4. Verified fix locally.

signals.topic: hookify Write tool silently bypasses event:file security rules — action:block ineffective
signals.summary: Rules with event:file in hookify never fire for the Write tool because rule_engine.py reads new_string field which Write doesn't use (it sends content instead). Net effect: action:block rules guarding file content (hardcoded credentials, public registry URLs, SSL bypass patterns) provide zero enforcement when Claude uses Write instead of Edit. Users relying on hookify for security guardrails are silently unprotected.
aliases: hookify security rule ineffective Write tool
signals.review_reason: Critical security feature unavailability: hookify's content policy enforcement is silently bypassed when Claude uses Write. Users relying on these rules for credential detection or content policy are unprotected without any warning. This is not a UX degradation — security rules provide zero enforcement.

source_issues.title: hookify: Write tool silently bypasses event:file rules (action:block ineffective)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction provided with exact test case showing Edit tool blocked correctly but Write tool passes through. Root cause identified in rule_engine.py _extract_field method. Fix provided. Impact: any event:file rule with action:block is silently ineffective for Write operations.

signals.topic: Tutorial references retired/deprecated Claude Haiku 3 model, causing tutorial instructions to fail or produce unexpected results for users
signals.summary: The interactive tutorial still references Claude Haiku 3, which has been retired. Users following the tutorial will encounter errors or confusion as the model is no longer available, degrading the learning experience and blocking successful completion of the tutorial exercises.
aliases: tutorial content not updated after model deprecation
signals.review_reason: This is a user-impacting issue: a retired model in tutorial content means users following the exercises will encounter failures or unexpected behavior when attempting to use Haiku 3, blocking successful completion of the tutorial. Count=1 and single-repo limits priority to P2. Not excluded as it has clear user impact evidence (tutorial instructions reference a model that is no longer available).

source_issues.title: Tutorial using Haiku 3- needs update
source_issues.evidence: User reports tutorial still uses the recently-retired Claude Haiku 3 and needs updating to 4.5. Users following the tutorial would get errors/failures since the referenced model is retired.

signals.topic: document-skills plugin loads all 17 skills instead of only the 4 declared in marketplace.json
signals.summary: When installing the document-skills plugin, all 17 skills from the repo are loaded instead of only the 4 declared in marketplace.json. The plugin loader loads every skill directory in the cache path without filtering against the skills array in marketplace.json, causing incorrect skill availability and namespace pollution.
aliases: plugin loader does not filter skills by marketplace.json declaration
wrong skills exposed after plugin install
signals.review_reason: This is a functional defect with clear user impact: users who install document-skills expecting only 4 document-processing skills instead get 17 unrelated skills (including claude-api, mcp-builder, etc.). The root cause is identified as the plugin loader not filtering skill directories against marketplace.json declarations. This pollutes the skill namespace and misleads users about what the plugin provides.

source_issues.title: document-skills plugin loads all skills from repo instead of only declared ones in marketplace.json
source_issues.evidence: Installing document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills exposes 17 skills instead of the 4 declared (xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf). Extra skills include algorithmic-art, brand-guidelines, claude-api, mcp-builder, etc. Root cause: plugin loader loads all directories in the cache path without filtering by marketplace.json skills array.

signals.topic: pdf skill does not warn about pdftotext -layout column drift on multi-page positional tables, leading to extraction failures and OOM
signals.summary: The pdf skill recommends pdftotext -layout for positional 'tables' (text positioned at fixed x/y coordinates without PDF table structure), but does not warn that pdftotext rescales character-column widths per page based on the widest line on that page. This causes column positions to differ across pages, breaking naive parsers on continuation pages, and can lead to OOM on very large documents (~3000+ pages) due to pdfplumber per-page cache without explicit flushing.
aliases: pdf positional table extraction fails on multi-page documents
pdftotext layout mode gives inconsistent column widths across pages
signals.review_reason: This is a real user pain point: users trying to extract positional tables from multi-page PDFs encounter silent column misalignment on continuation pages and possible OOM on large documents. The skill provides no guidance on this common failure case (positional tables without PDF structure), leaving users to independently discover the pdftotext limitation and find the pdfplumber.extract_words() workaround. Priority is P2 because count=1 and it is a documentation/guidance gap rather than a full workflow block.

source_issues.title: pdf skill: `pdftotext -layout` column-drift on multi-page positional "tables"
source_issues.evidence: Multi-page PDFs with positional tables (common from MS Access exports, schema dumps, auto-generated reports) cause pdftotext -layout to rescale column widths per page based on per-page widest line (header/footer), leading to column drift. A real case hit OOM at ~3000 pages of a 5500-page document due to pdfplumber per-page cache without flush. The skill's Quick Reference / Extract Tables section does not mention this failure mode or the reliable alternative (pdfplumber.extract_words() with physical x-coordinates).

signals.topic: Queued/interjected message is silently deleted when user tries to interrupt Goose processing
signals.summary: When Goose is actively generating a response and user sends an interjection (queued message), clicking the Send button on the queued card immediately stops processing AND permanently deletes the queued message. This breaks the interjection/interrupt feature entirely — the message is never delivered and must be manually retyped. 100% reproducible.
aliases: queued card send button deletes message instead of delivering
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：interjection（打断/插话）功能完全失效，用户消息被静默删除而不是发送。这是 Goose 核心交互功能的严重回归，100%可复现，用户必须手动重打消息。

source_issues.title: Queued message interrupt kills processing and deletes the queued message
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible: clicking Send on queued interjection card immediately stops processing and permanently deletes the queued message — never delivered, user must manually retype. Affects core interrupt/interjection workflow.

signals.topic: MCP elicitation user response not delivered — Goose Desktop hangs indefinitely
signals.summary: After a user submits a response to an MCP elicitation prompt in Goose Desktop UI, the response is not successfully sent back to the MCP server, causing Goose Desktop to hang forever with no further interaction possible. A related elicitation crash (SSE-collision) was partially fixed but the hang persists.
aliases: elicitation response not delivered causing hang
Goose Desktop hangs after elicitation submission
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户在 MCP elicitation 对话框提交回复后，Goose Desktop 永远挂起，无法继续任何操作。这是关键功能不可用的严重问题。

source_issues.title: Race condition while connecting to MCP servers & elicitation errors
source_issues.evidence: After users respond to elicitation in Goose Desktop, the result is not successfully delivered to the MCP server, causing Goose Desktop to hang forever. Demonstrated with screen recording and screenshots showing the hang state.

signals.topic: Streaming response parse failure when LLM returns null function arguments in tool_calls delta chunk
signals.summary: When an LLM (e.g. DeepSeek V4 Pro) returns a streaming chunk with null `function.arguments` in a tool_calls delta, Goose fails to parse the chunk with an explicit type mismatch error, crashing the streaming pipeline.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：LLM 流式响应解析直接抛出异常，导致工具调用管道崩溃，中间响应失败。这在特定模型（如 DeepSeek V4 Pro）上是确定性复现。

source_issues.title: Failed to parse streaming chunk: invalid type: null when llm response tool_calls function arguments is null
source_issues.evidence: Goose fails with explicit parse error 'invalid type: null' when a streaming LLM response contains a tool_calls delta chunk where function.arguments is null. This crashes the streaming pipeline mid-response.

signals.topic: Streamable HTTP MCP extension timeout not respected on Linux — calls reset after ~30s
signals.summary: On Linux, Streamable HTTP MCP tool calls fail after ~30 seconds even when the extension config specifies a much larger timeout (e.g. timeout: 300). The underlying reqwest HTTP client's TCP_USER_TIMEOUT defaults to 30 seconds on Linux and is not overridden by Goose, causing premature connection resets before the configured timeout is reached.
aliases: MCP streamable HTTP timeout ignored on Linux
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：Linux 环境下长时 MCP 任务（>30秒）在 Goose 配置的更大超时限制生效前就被底层 socket 强制重置，导致复杂任务（如 Elastic Agent Builder 工具）无法完成。

source_issues.title: Streamable HTTP MCP calls on Linux may reset after ~30s despite larger extension timeout
source_issues.evidence: Linux reqwest client defaults TCP_USER_TIMEOUT to 30s, which fires before Goose's configured extension timeout (e.g. 300s). Legitimate long-running MCP tools (e.g. Elastic Agent Builder) are killed prematurely on Linux, blocking workflows that require >30s execution time.

signals.topic: Default max_output_tokens=4096 silently truncates long responses for local/unknown model providers
signals.summary: When using local inference providers (llama_swap, lmstudio, etc.) or any model not in Goose's known list, max_output_tokens defaults to 4096. This limit is passed to the OpenAI-compatible API and truncates nontrivial responses mid-stream. The user has no indication this is happening — the model just stops and the task appears to fail. Workaround requires manually editing config.yaml.
aliases: default token limit too low for local models
model responses truncated due to hardcoded 4096 max_tokens
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败：本地推理用户（非标准模型）在使用复杂任务时输出被静默截断，模型中途停止，用户完全不知道为什么。这导致本地模型的复杂任务几乎无法完成。

source_issues.title: Default max_output_tokens of 4096 is unreasonably low
source_issues.evidence: Local providers (llama_swap, lmstudio) with unknown models get max_tokens=4096 by default, causing nontrivial responses to be silently truncated. User has no indication why — model stops mid-task and complex tasks fail entirely. Average user cannot diagnose without deep knowledge.

signals.topic: XPath brittleness causes ActCache failures and forces costly LLM re-inference
signals.summary: Stagehand's reliance on XPath-based element targeting causes ActCache to break when minor DOM changes occur (e.g., inserted div wrappers, reordered elements), leading to unnecessary action retries and forced LLM re-inference, resulting in both quality degradation and monetary cost.
aliases: ActCache invalidation due to DOM changes
signals.review_reason: 虽然该 issue 以 feature request 形式提出，但其核心描述的根因是真实的用户痛点：XPath 的脆弱性导致 ActCache 在页面结构微小变化时失效，用户被迫重新触发 LLM 推理，产生额外成本（re-inference = 金钱损失）和体验下降（缓存动作仍然失败）。Issue 明确引用 #1434 作为佐证，说明并非个例。符合'主流程体验下降'和'成本损失'两个痛点条件。标记为 P1 而非 P0 是因为单仓单 issue，且该 feature 为 opt-in，默认行为不变，影响范围有限。

source_issues.title: Support Stable Selectors (IDs, Data Attributes, CSS)
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states XPath brittleness breaks ActCache on minor DOM changes, causing unnecessary retries and LLM re-inference. References issue #1434 which documents XPath brittleness causing action failures. This represents a real-world cost impact (LLM re-inference = monetary cost) and a main-flow quality degradation (action failures even when target element unchanged).

signals.topic: LoopDetectionMiddleware warn injection breaks OpenAI/Moonshot tool-call pairing — causes unrecoverable 400 errors and workflow interruption
signals.summary: LoopDetectionMiddleware 在 after_model 中注入 HumanMessage 警告，打断了 tool_call/tool_message 的顺序，导致 Moonshot/OpenAI 等严格 provider 返回 400 'tool_call_ids did not have response messages'，对话不可恢复。RFC #2517 已将其列为验收标准中的必须修复项。历史上已反复报告（#2029, #2255, #2293, #2304, #2319, #2511, #2662）。
aliases: 循环检测导致 400 错误
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断型 bug：OpenAI/Moonshot 用户的工具调用工作流在循环检测触发时直接 400 失败且不可恢复，历史累计 8 次独立报告，RFC #2517 已将其列为必须修复的验收标准，影响所有使用严格 tool-call provider 的用户。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Loop-detection warn injection breaks tool-call pairing on OpenAI/Moonshot — temporary mitigation for v2.0-m1
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: after_model returns HumanMessage between AIMessage(tool_calls=...) and ToolMessage responses. Moonshot validator requires tool_calls→tool_messages adjacent. 10-seed repro: 5/10 failures → 0/10 after fix. Cites 7 prior reports.

source_issues.title: LLM request failed: Error code: 400
source_issues.evidence: Exact error: 'An assistant message with tool_calls must be followed by tool messages responding to each tool_call_id. (insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message)'. User reports 400 on first chat turn.

signals.topic: MiniMax M2.7 subagent LLM calls consistently fail with HTTP 400 error code 2013
signals.summary: factory.py 在 subagent 创建时因 thinking_enabled=False 错误注入 reasoning_effort + thinking:disabled 参数，MiniMax API 不接受这些参数导致所有 subagent 调用 400 失败，而 lead agent 因 thinking_enabled=True 正常工作。影响所有使用 MiniMax M2.7 subagent 的用户。
aliases: MiniMax subagent thinking 参数错误
signals.review_reason: Subagent 功能对 MiniMax 用户完全不可用，3 个独立 issue 确认根因相同（factory.py thinking 参数注入错误），lead agent 正常但 subagent 全灭，影响所有使用 MiniMax + subagent 的用户。

source_issues.title: Subagent LLM calls fail with 400 (error 2013) when using MiniMax M2.7 via OpenAI-compatible gateway
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis: factory.py auto-injects reasoning_effort:minimal + thinking:{type:disabled} for subagents. MiniMax rejects these. Lead agent succeeds (thinking_enabled=True → accepted params). 3 subagents all fail identically.

source_issues.title: MiniMax-M2.7 model returns 400 'user name must be consistent (2013)' when invoking subagents
source_issues.evidence: Body=null but title confirms the subagent error on MiniMax direct API.

source_issues.title: MiniMax models return 400 'invalid chat setting (2013)' when subagent is invoked
source_issues.evidence: Body=null; duplicate confirmation of subagent 400 on MiniMax via OpenAI-compatible proxy.

aliases: make start frontend crash missing config
signals.review_reason: 生产部署完全阻断：frontend 容器因 config 缺失直接崩溃，2 个独立报告确认，所有通过 make start 部署的用户都无法正常使用系统。

source_issues.title: frontend容器报错
source_issues.evidence: Error: 'invalid_type, expected array, received undefined, path trustedOrigins' — SSR crash in Next.js, user cannot access frontend at all after make up/start.

source_issues.title: [runtime] make start 后，后端接口报500错误
source_issues.evidence: Same trustedOrigins + internalGatewayUrl undefined errors in production mode. User shows full make start output and screenshot of crash.

signals.review_reason: Telegram 集成关键功能断裂，所有 Telegram 用户使用 /models 命令时 401 失败，代码审查确认 manager.py 缺少 auth headers，是明确的代码遗漏 bug。

source_issues.evidence: HTTP 401 on http://localhost:8001/api/models. manager.py#L1000 missing headers=create_internal_auth_headers() compared to other similar calls.

signals.topic: Thinking mode (reasoning models) breaks tool calls — agent retries with 'missing required parameter' errors across multiple providers and model families

The agent reports 'Cline tried to use search_files without value for required parameter regex' and keeps retrying. Affects multiple reasoning model families. Reverting to 3.81.0 resolves it.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断(high-frequency workflow failure): count=3,涉及deepseek-reasoner和Kimi两个主流推理模型,工具调用全部失败并陷入重试循环。用户已确认退回3.81.0可修复,证明是3.82.0引入的回归性问题,影响所有使用推理模型的用户核心工作流。

source_issues.title: 3.82.0 tool calls fail with Deepseek v4-flash (Thinking)
source_issues.evidence: Frequent 'Cline tried to use search_files without value for required parameter regex' errors with deepseek-reasoner. Reverting to 3.81.0 fixes the problem.

source_issues.title: "invalid_arguments" / unterminated string
source_issues.evidence: Chat terminates with 'Unterminated string in JSON' error with Kimi 2.6. Tool response parsing fails during thinking model interaction.

signals.topic: Cline hangs at 'Thinking...' phase indefinitely after executing terminal commands, completely blocking the main agent workflow
signals.summary: In v3.82.0, after a terminal command executes successfully, Cline gets stuck at the 'Thinking...' phase and never proceeds. Users have waited over 1 hour with no resolution, making the entire agent workflow unusable. This is a regression from v3.81.0 and affects the primary usage loop.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断(high-severity regression): 用户在核心使用循环(执行终端命令后等待AI响应)中被完全卡住超过1小时,严重影响生产力。Issue明确标注为回归,说明v3.82.0引入的严重阻断性问题。

source_issues.title: Cline v3.82.0 hangs indefinitely at "Thinking..." after executing terminal commands
source_issues.evidence: User waited over 1 hour with Cline stuck at 'Thinking...' phase after terminal command executed successfully. Main agent workflow completely blocked. Regression from previous version.

signals.topic: DeepSeek API provider fails to complete basic file editing/creation tasks with JSON parsing errors
signals.summary: DeepSeek API provider is operational but breaks the fundamental file editing workflow. Even simple tasks like creating a file or any editing operation fail due to JSON parsing errors in the tool response. Users cannot complete any coding task through the DeepSeek provider.

DeepSeek API provider file operations broken

source_issues.title: Deepseek API provider issue: Invalid input for tool read_files: JSON parsing failed
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek API provider can respond but even basic file creation/editing tasks cannot be completed. Tool calls fail with JSON parsing errors, making the entire coding workflow non-functional for DeepSeek users.

signals.topic: Windows-specific: Removing one MCP server configuration deletes ALL configured MCP servers
signals.summary: On Windows, when a user removes just one MCP server from their configuration, all other configured MCP servers are silently deleted. This is a catastrophic data loss bug that affects all MCP server users on Windows. A video demonstration confirms the behavior.
aliases: Windows MCP server deletion all servers
MCP server config wipe on delete
signals.review_reason: 数据丢失灾难性bug(catastrophic data loss): Windows平台删除单个MCP Server配置时会静默删除所有其他MCP Server,视频证据确凿。这是严重的数据完整性破坏,count虽为1但用户证据充分(附带录像),平台覆盖所有Windows用户,达到P0标准。

source_issues.title: [Windows Specific] Cline: Removing one MCP server deletes all configured MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: Removing any single MCP server causes all other MCP servers to be deleted. Video evidence provided. Affects all MCP users on Windows with multiple servers configured. Data loss severity.

signals.topic: CLI run_commands tool silently times out at 30s with misleading error — wastes tokens and causes agent to misdiagnose long-running tasks
signals.summary: The run_commands tool has a hard 30-second wall-clock timeout. When exceeded, it returns a misleading 'Command failed' error instead of indicating a timeout. This causes the AI agent to waste significant time and tokens attempting workarounds (nohup, screen, scripts) for tasks that actually completed successfully in the background.
signals.review_reason: 显著成本损失(token waste + workflow confusion): 虽然count=1,但问题影响所有CLI长期运行任务场景,明确造成token浪费('wasted tokens on unnecessary debugging')并导致agent反复尝试错误解决方式。30s硬编码超时限制了所有编译、测试、ML训练等合法长期任务的执行,是CLI主流程上的体验下降。

source_issues.title: 'run_commands' tool silently times out at 30s with misleading error — causes agent confusion and wasted tokens on long-running tasks
source_issues.evidence: Commands taking >30s return misleading 'Command failed' error. Agent wastes tokens on unnecessary debugging and workarounds. Process often still running in background with correct output, but agent cannot distinguish. Explicit token and time waste documented.

signals.topic: IntelliJ/JetBrains IDE 中 End 键被 Continue 插件劫持，编辑体验受损

signals.review_reason: 核心编辑体验受损：End 键是日常最高频的编辑操作之一，插件劫持导致每次使用需按两次，严重影响编辑流畅性，属于体验显著下降。且同一根因已出现 2 条独立 issue。

source_issues.title: IntelliJ plugin hijacks End key
source_issues.evidence: Windows 11 + Continue 1.0.67 + IntelliJ 2026.1.1 环境下，在 .toml 文件中按 End 键时光标不移动，需按两次才能到达行尾。插件在无自动补全建议时仍拦截按键输入。

source_issues.title: Interferes with `End` key pressing
source_issues.evidence: 与 #12302 同一根因，YouTrack 工单 IJPL-244168 记录了完整的复现步骤和视频证据。

source_issues.evidence: 新注册账号在 hub.continue.dev 登录时返回 401 Unauthorized，错误信息为 'Not authenticated (user missing)'，用户完全无法访问 Hub 仪表板。官方支持邮箱不可达。

signals.topic: 代码自动补全功能完全失效，Ollama 模型下无任何提示

signals.topic: AI 编辑建议后用户输入 follow-up 导致编辑器与 AI 状态不同步，后续 diff 失效

signals.review_reason: 会话状态不一致问题：AI 对文件状态的理解与实际不一致，会导致后续所有 AI 操作都基于错误状态，产生无效或错误的代码变更，属于会话级逻辑缺陷。

source_issues.title: Responding with a follow-up when AI suggests an edit results in desync
source_issues.evidence: 用户描述了完整的复现步骤：向 AI 询问编辑后输入 follow-up，编辑实际不执行但界面标记为已接受，导致 AI 后续输出的 diff 失效，长文件下影响更大。

signals.topic: 重复打印 'Info: Tracing is disabled' 消息导致体验骚扰
signals.summary: 用户在使用 crewAI 时，控制台反复打印 'Info: Tracing is disabled' 提示信息，累计打印 100 次，严重影响使用体验和日志可读性，用户明确表示不愿被反复骚扰。

source_issues.title: [BUG] I can not stop the "Info: Tracing is disabled." nagging.
source_issues.evidence: 用户在控制台中观察到 'Info: Tracing is disabled.' 被打印约 100 次，影响日志可读性且无法屏蔽。

signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断——用户组合多个官方特性（ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context）时 Crew 直接崩溃，TypeError 表明 Pydantic 模型对象被错误地传递给了需要 JSON 字符串的函数。这是关键功能不可用的明确证据。

source_issues.title: [BUG] TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not <PydanticModel> when combining ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context
source_issues.evidence: 用户同时使用 ConditionalTask、output_pydantic、自定义 guardrail 和 context 时，crewAI 抛出 TypeError，导致 Crew 无法正常完成。

signals.topic: BrightData SERP 工具因 JavaScript 模板语法错误导致所有搜索查询 URL 损坏

aliases: brightdata serp search broken URL format
signals.review_reason: BrightData 搜索工具 URL 模板语法错误导致所有搜索查询均生成形如 '?q=$AI%20news' 的错误 URL，Google/Bing/Yandex 三大搜索引擎全部受影响。用户提供了清晰的代码对比（`${query}` vs `{query}`）和复现步骤。BrightDataSearchTool 是 crewAI 官方集成工具，该 bug 导致整个搜索功能不可用。

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: 代码中 f"https://www.google.com/search?q=${query}" 产生字面量 '$' 前缀，导致所有搜索 URL 损坏。用户提供了代码对比和 Python shell 验证。

signals.topic: 异步工作流中使用 akickoff() 时因同步 LLM 调用阻塞事件循环导致超时/挂起
signals.summary: 在使用 akickoff() 启动的异步工作流中，当 Task 设置了 output_json 或 output_pydantic 时，converter 模块调用同步 self.llm.call() 而非 await llm.acall()，导致事件循环被阻塞，引发异步工作流超时或挂起。
aliases: async akickoff sync LLM call blocking event loop
signals.review_reason: 异步工作流中调用同步 LLM 方法是主流程阻断性问题——事件循环被阻塞会导致整个异步流程挂起或超时。这是 async/await 使用中的关键反模式，用户提供了具体的代码路径和示例引用。

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous `call()` on LLM from asynchronous workflow in `_export_output` / converter
source_issues.evidence: 异步工作流使用 akickoff() 且 Task 有 output_json/output_pydantic 时，converter 模块中同步调用 self.llm.call() 阻塞事件循环。用户引用了具体代码行（task.py L605/L1258/L1023）。

signals.topic: LLM 响应处理中缺失 'messages' 键时抛出混淆性 KeyError 而非明确的 ValueError
signals.summary: 在 crewai/llm.py 的 _handle_non_streaming_response() 和 _ahandle_non_streaming_response() 中，当 params 缺少 'messages' 键且设置了 response_model 时，代码先正确抛出 ValueError，但随后在调用 _handle_emit_call_events 时又因直接访问 params["messages"] 而产生混淆性 KeyError，导致错误信息不清晰且流程控制混乱。
aliases: missing messages KeyError vs ValueError confusion
signals.review_reason: LLM 核心模块中的 KeyError 会导致异步任务崩溃且错误信息不清晰（混淆性 KeyError vs 预期 ValueError），影响依赖 response_model 的异步 LLM 调用流程。虽然该路径较边缘（需要特定参数组合），但错误信息混淆性高，会显著增加用户调试难度。

source_issues.title: [BUG] KeyError when params missing 'messages' key in _handle_non_streaming_response
source_issues.evidence: 代码在 llm.py L1220/L1364 处直接访问 params['messages']，在特定条件（response_model 设置但 messages 缺失）下产生 KeyError。用户明确指出应使用前面已提取的 messages 变量。

signals.topic: CLI falls back to binary name as pattern causing misleading error when -p is omitted with positional args or --transcript
signals.summary: When fabric-ai is invoked without -p but with positional args or -y URL --transcript, it falls back to using os.Args[0] as the pattern name, producing the confusing error "pattern 'fabric-ai' not found". This sends users in the wrong debugging direction (checking installation, Homebrew packaging) and breaks the README zsh yt() helper which omits -p.
aliases: binary name used as pattern fallback
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime bug that causes CLI commands to fail with a misleading error message, sending users on the wrong debugging path. While not a full block (users can work around by adding -p), it directly degrades the main CLI interaction experience and breaks documented shell integration examples, meeting the threshold for a user pain point.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Misleading "pattern '<binary-name>' not found" when no pattern is specified, plus README zsh yt() example is broken since #1960
source_issues.evidence: fabric-ai update and fabric-ai -y <url> --transcript both fail with misleading error; yt() shell helper broken since #1960; user misdiagnoses as install/packaging issue

signals.topic: Opus-4.7 model rejects temperature parameter causing 400 Bad Request and request failures
signals.summary: When using the Opus-4.7 model, the Anthropic API rejects requests with a 400 Bad Request because temperature is deprecated for this model. Fabric does not strip temperature from the request payload for this model, causing complete request failures.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime bug that directly causes API request failures with 400 Bad Request errors. The request cannot complete at all with Opus-4.7, representing a clear blocking condition for users of that model. The root cause is identifiable and fixable (need to strip temperature for Opus-4.7), making it a genuine user pain point.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Opus-4.7 temperature deprecated for this model
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 Bad Request: "temperature is deprecated for this model"; request completely fails; confirmed on macOS with Homebrew install v1.4.451

signals.topic: Groq chat.completions API rejects Fabric payloads when message array ends with system role instead of user role
signals.summary: Fabric constructs chat payloads where pattern instructions are concatenated with user input into a single system message, with no trailing user message. Groq's chat.completions API enforces that the last message role must be 'user' and rejects such payloads with a 400 error, breaking many built-in patterns (e.g., summarize) for all Groq users.
aliases: Groq last message role must be user
Groq vendor adapter message role issue
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-runtime bug that causes API request failures for all Groq users across many built-in patterns. The Groq API returns a 400 error, completely blocking the main workflow (summarize, and any pattern using system.md + INPUT). Clear user impact with reproducible steps, making it a genuine user pain point despite count=1.

source_issues.title: Groq chat.completions rejects Fabric payload when pattern input becomes a system message (last role must be 'user')
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with printf piped to fabric -p summarize --vendor Groq; API returns 400 Bad Request with 'last message role must be user'; affects all patterns that place INPUT in system.md

signals.topic: HttpsProxyAgent crash when using Vertex AI with HTTP_PROXY environment variables
signals.summary: Gemini CLI crashes fatally with 'TypeError: HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor' when Vertex AI auth is used alongside HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY environment variables, rendering the CLI completely unusable for proxy users.
signals.review_reason: Fatal CLI crash that completely blocks the main workflow for any user using Vertex AI auth behind a proxy. This is not an edge case — proxy usage is standard in many enterprise/CI environments. The crash occurs during the authentication phase, making the entire CLI unusable for affected users.

source_issues.title: Bug: "HttpsProxyAgent is not a constructor" crash when using Vertex AI with HTTP_PROXY environment variables
source_issues.evidence: Fatal TypeError crash during auth phase. Root cause is CommonJS/ESM export mismatch in bundled gemini-cli JS chunk causing https-proxy-agent to export an object instead of a constructor class. Workaround of clearing proxy env vars exists but blocks legitimate proxy use cases.

signals.topic: YOLO mode still prompts for confirmation on shell commands with redirection operators
signals.summary: In interactive YOLO mode, run_shell_command calls with redirection operators (>, >>, <, <<) incorrectly display a confirmation prompt instead of being auto-approved as YOLO mode promises. The policy engine or UI layer bypasses the YOLO wildcard rule for redirected commands.
aliases: YOLO mode redirection confirmation prompt bug
signals.review_reason: Breaks the core promise of YOLO mode — auto-approval of all commands without user prompts. When a user intentionally enables YOLO to avoid interruptions, they still get blocked by confirmation dialogs for redirected commands. This is a clear UX contract violation that defeats the purpose of the feature.

source_issues.title: bug: redirection in run_shell_command still prompts for approval in YOLO mode (interactive)
source_issues.evidence: YOLO mode is explicitly designed to auto-approve all commands, but redirected shell commands still surface the 'Redirection detected' confirmation panel. Deep root cause analysis provided pointing to PolicyEngine.checkShellCommand or ruleMatches mode-matching issues. Reproducible in interactive model loop.

signals.topic: Invalid Auto Memory inbox patches become invisible and non-dismissible
signals.summary: Auto Memory silently skips invalid memory patches (malformed, no hunks, out-of-root) during processing, making them invisible in the /memory inbox UI. Users cannot apply or dismiss these stale artifacts, and the background extractor keeps re-feeding them into future extraction prompts.
aliases: stale memory patch artifacts cannot be dismissed
signals.review_reason: A core feature (/memory inbox) becomes functionally broken when invalid patches accumulate invisibly. Users lose the ability to review and manage their memory patches, and the background extractor is polluted with stale artifacts. This directly degrades the Auto Memory system's reliability and user trust.

source_issues.title: Surface or quarantine invalid Auto Memory inbox patches
source_issues.evidence: Invalid patch files accumulate invisibly in the inbox. Users cannot dismiss or manage them via /memory inbox. The background extractor repeatedly processes these stale artifacts, degrading extraction quality over time. Explicit acceptance criteria defined for fix.

signals.topic: Auto Memory retries low-signal sessions indefinitely, wasting extraction capacity and cost
signals.summary: Auto Memory's extraction agent skips sessions it deems low-signal without marking them as processed, causing the same sessions to be re-surfaced on every extraction run. Combined with the 30-minute throttle, this creates persistent wasted background work and unpredictable cost accumulation.
signals.review_reason: Causes predictable cost waste and unpredictable extraction behavior. Every extraction run wastes capacity on sessions already evaluated as low-signal, reducing the effective throughput of the memory extraction system. This is a direct cost loss for paying users with Auto Memory enabled.

source_issues.title: Stop Auto Memory from retrying low-signal sessions indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: processedSessionKeys only tracks successful read_file activity. Skipped sessions remain unprocessed and re-surfaced every extraction interval. The 30-minute throttle reduces frequency but does not prevent the repeated work. Documented as a background reliability and cost-control issue.

signals.topic: Chat corruption bug in context manager causing data integrity issues
signals.summary: A bug in the context manager causes chat data corruption, leading to data integrity failures in active CLI sessions.
signals.review_reason: Chat data corruption is a critical data integrity issue. Even without detailed body content, the issue title explicitly identifies a corruption bug in the context manager, and it has been triaged as a valid bug. Corruption in active chat sessions can lead to lost work and trust in the CLI's reliability.

source_issues.title: Fix chat corruption bug with context manager
source_issues.evidence: Issue title explicitly states 'chat corruption bug' related to context manager. Labeled for triage by maintainers, indicating it is a recognized issue requiring investigation.

signals.topic: MCP tool calls logged as python_interpreter in agent memory, preventing structured tool call tracking
signals.summary: When using MCP tools via ToolCollection with CodeAgent, the agent.memory.get_full_steps() API logs all MCP tool invocations as generic `python_interpreter` calls, obscuring the actual MCP tool name and its kwargs. Users cannot retrieve a structured list of which MCP tools were called and with what arguments, making end-to-end testing and debugging difficult. The workaround of monkey-patching each tool's forward method is non-obvious and fragile.
aliases: MCP calls appear as python_interpreter in memory
cannot extract MCP tool kwargs from agent history
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine usability bug that breaks the agent's introspection API for MCP tool users. The agent.memory.get_full_steps() contract is broken for MCP tools — it returns opaque python_interpreter entries instead of structured MCP call metadata — which directly blocks end-to-end testing workflows. Single occurrence is noted; elevated from P2 because the bug violates a core API contract and the monkey-patching workaround is non-trivial.

source_issues.title: BUG: MCP tools calls gets logged inside the Python Code intepreter
source_issues.evidence: User reports that agent.memory.get_full_steps() returns python_interpreter calls for MCP tools, making it impossible to retrieve the actual MCP tool name and kwargs. Provides reproduction code and notes the only workaround is monkey-patching each tool's forward method individually.

signals.topic: Codex provider integration fails to respect 'never stop' instruction, breaking interactive session functionality
signals.summary: Codex integration with autoresearch ignores the 'never stop' instruction, causing the agent to halt prematurely in interactive sessions. This blocks the primary use case of interactive agent execution, unlike Claude provider which works correctly.
signals.review_reason: This is a functional failure of a key LLM provider integration (Codex) that directly blocks the primary interactive session workflow. Author is the repo owner, providing authoritative confirmation. Unlike Claude which supports /loop correctly, Codex users cannot use the core interactive agent feature — this is a clear user-facing workflow break with 40 comments indicating community relevance. Not P0 only because count=1 with single-repo impact, lacking broader cross-repo evidence.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: Author (karpathy, repo owner) confirms Codex ignores instruction to never stop, causing agent to stop prematurely in interactive sessions. 40 comments indicate active community interest. No workaround exists for Codex users — only Claude provider (via /loop) works correctly.

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.ls silently returns empty LsResult on FileNotFoundError/PermissionError instead of propagating error, misleading agents
signals.summary: ls on invalid or inaccessible paths returns identical empty result as an empty directory, poisoning agent context with false information.
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation: agents receive false 'empty directory' signal on invalid paths, leading to wrong path assumptions and poisoned context. User explicitly reports inability to self-reflect. Consistent pattern: ls errors are swallowed while read/grep/glob correctly propagate errors.

source_issues.title: fix(sdk): `BaseSandbox.ls` silently swallows `FileNotFoundError`/`PermissionError`, returning empty `LsResult` on invalid paths
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows ls on non-existent path returns `LsResult(entries=[], error=None)` identical to an empty directory. Contrast: read() correctly sets error. User states 'my agent's context is poisoned with false information, therefore not able to self-reflect properly'.

source_issues.title: fix(sdk): `BaseSandbox.ls` silently swallows `FileNotFoundError`/`PermissionError`, returning empty `LsResult` on invalid paths
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report from same author (keenborder786) filed 30 minutes earlier without bug label. Internal comment indicates same underlying bug.

signals.topic: read_file kwarg mismatch: tool description examples use `path` but schema declares `file_path`, causing tool call failures and retry waste
signals.summary: Tool description examples use `path` as kwarg name but the schema declares `file_path`, causing models to emit invalid calls that trip Pydantic validation, wasting agent turns on retry.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: agent tool calls fail and require retry. Direct cost impact through wasted turns. Reproducible across multiple versions.

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware: read_file description shows examples with wrong kwarg name (`path` vs schema's `file_path`)
source_issues.evidence: Tool schema declares `file_path` but description examples use `path` as kwarg. Models trained on description emit `read_file(path=...)` and trip Pydantic `Field required: file_path`. Wastes a turn on retry. Affects every released version (0.4.1 through 0.6.0a1).

signals.topic: FilesystemMiddleware crashes with 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'error' when backend WriteResult returns None
signals.summary: Middleware crashes with AttributeError when a custom backend returns a WriteResult that the middleware does not expect, blocking agent execution entirely.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: agent execution crashes entirely when using a custom backend that returns a WriteResult the middleware does not expect. Clear blocker for users integrating custom backends.

source_issues.evidence: External user implementing BackendProtocol with Postgres backend hit `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'error'` at filesystem.py line 1030 when `awrite` returns a WriteResult. Stack trace shows crash during actual agent execution.

signals.topic: SkillsMiddleware preloading all skill files into LangGraph state causes state bloat and checkpoint overhead

aliases: skill file preloading bloats checkpoint state
signals.review_reason: Significant UX/cost impact: serialized state grows with every skill file, causing checkpoint overhead and LangSmith trace bloat on every turn. Not blocking but causes measurable performance/cost degradation in long sessions.

source_issues.title: SkillsMiddleware progressive disclosure broken: preloaded files bloat LangGraph state
source_issues.evidence: User reports skill metadata correctly injected into system prompt (progressive disclosure) but all preloaded files still serialized into LangGraph state. Describes 'no-win situation': preloading gives full content bloat, not preloading breaks read_file for resource files. User on deepagents 0.5.7 confirmed this.
