signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out
signals.summary: LangGraph checkpoint serialization (MemorySaver, SqliteSaver, PostgresSaver) uses full Pydantic metadata via dumpd() on every write, causing 85% storage overhead and significant context-window token inflation. No opt-out path exists.
signals.review_reason: This is a cost loss issue — users incur compounding storage overhead across every checkpoint write, directly inflating Postgres/Redis bills at scale and expanding context window usage. The overhead is silent (no exception raised) but measurable on every graph turn, making it a persistent cost drain rather than a one-time failure.

source_issues.title: LangGraph checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path
source_issues.evidence: A 16-turn ReAct agent with 65 messages produces a checkpoint of 21,850 bytes under MemorySaver. The same state encoded with a binary pooling serializer compresses to 3,217 bytes — 85.3% storage overhead (6.79x) compounding into Postgres/Redis storage costs. Token overhead: 5,764 tokens vs 3,587 semantic tokens = 37.8% inflation in every context window.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators silently return wrong query results due to lexicographic comparison
signals.summary: PostgresStore filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) perform text-based comparison on numeric values, silently returning incorrect results — e.g. score=9 incorrectly passes score>=$gte:10.
aliases: lexicographic vs numeric comparison in PostgresStore
signals.review_reason: This bug causes silent data integrity failures: users filtering for numeric thresholds get wrong results with no error or warning. Items with score=9 pass a score>=10 filter. This can directly lead to incorrect business decisions based on corrupted query results — a critical feature failure for any application using PostgresStore with numeric filters.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: In PostgreSQL: '9' >= '10' is True (text ordering) — items with score=9 incorrectly pass a {"score": {"$gte": 10}} filter. Filter SQL uses ILIKE/Text instead of numeric comparison operators.

signals.topic: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
signals.summary: PostgresSaver.setup() and PostgresStore.setup() raise ActiveSqlTransaction error because they use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which cannot run inside any transaction block — blocking atomic multi-tenant provisioning.
aliases: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in transaction block
signals.review_reason: This blocks atomic provisioning flows for multi-tenant applications where checkpoint table setup must roll back together with tenant schema creation. Users are forced to deviate from the upstream migration path and manage setup manually, creating fragility in production deployment pipelines.

source_issues.title: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
source_issues.evidence: psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. MIGRATIONS contains three CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statements (base.py L76/L79/L82), and Postgres rejects it even inside an empty transaction on a fresh table.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud causing 2-3x redundant work and cost
signals.summary: When tool calls exceed ~3 minutes on LangGraph Cloud, the system re-dispatches the call from the last checkpoint while the original is still running, completing both and doubling costs.
aliases: long running tool re-execution on cloud
silent tool call duplication on LangGraph Cloud
signals.review_reason: This causes direct and explicit cost multiplication (2-3x) for users with legitimate long-running tool calls — a billing anomaly caused by silent framework behavior. The duplication is consistent, reproducible, and affects every long-running tool call on LangGraph Cloud. The silent nature (no error raised, both executions succeed) means users may not notice until they review their billing. This is the clearest financial impact issue in the dataset.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: When a tool call takes longer than ~3 minutes on LangGraph Cloud, it gets silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both original and duplicate complete successfully, resulting in 2-3x redundant LLM calls and tool executions. Reproduced across langgraph 1.1.3–1.1.6, EU Cloud, Plus tier. The duplicate runs have identical tool call arguments (same content hash) and their own tools node but no preceding model node — indicating checkpoint re-trigger, not LLM re-decision.

signals.topic: Agent infinite loops until recursion limit error is hit, preventing task completion
signals.summary: Agents enter infinite loops in LangGraph 1.0.6+, hitting the recursion limit instead of stopping, even when the prompt clearly defines stop conditions.
aliases: recursion limit reached without stop condition
signals.review_reason: This blocks the main workflow — the agent cannot complete its task and hits the recursion limit instead, resulting in task failure. The regression from 0.6* to 1.0.6 means existing workflows break after an upgrade. This is a primary workflow failure affecting any agent that relies on natural stop conditions.

source_issues.title: LangGraph [1.0.6] Bug - Agent infinite looping until recursion limit error is hit
source_issues.evidence: Recursion limit of 20 reached without hitting a stop condition. The agent loops indefinitely despite clear evidence that the agent should be stopping based on the prompt given. User reports it worked in version 0.6* but breaks in 1.0.6, indicating a regression.

signals.topic: Multiple critical regressions in v1.14.0: API file upload broken, workflow restore button wipes draft canvas, agent editor fails to load, Notion OAuth dialog immediately dismisses
signals.summary: Dify v1.14.0 introduces multiple regressions affecting core workflows: the workflow restore button clears the draft when collaboration mode is disabled, the agent editor cannot be opened, the Notion OAuth configuration dialog disappears on interaction, and the API file upload is broken. All four issues are absent in v1.13.x.
signals.review_reason: 多维度退化：v1.14.0同时引入了4个退化，覆盖API层（文件上传）、编辑器UI（agent编辑器）、配置UI（Notion OAuth）和工作流编辑（restore按钮）。这些退化分布在用户最常用的核心功能路径上，表明1.14版本存在系统性的质量下滑。4个issue各自有独立复现路径但同版本引入，应当作为聚类痛点处理。

source_issues.title: [1.14.0] API file upload is broken, works fine in 1.13.0
source_issues.evidence: API file upload returns 400 invalid_param in 1.14.0, works in 1.13.0

source_issues.title: Workflow restore from top-right restore button clears draft when collaboration mode is disabled (1.14.0)
source_issues.evidence: Top-right workflow Restore button calls a different endpoint than the version item context menu Restore. In non-collaboration mode, the top-right button clears the draft canvas (shows empty) while reporting success. The correct path (version item menu → Restore) works.

source_issues.title: Agent editor cannot open.
source_issues.evidence: Creating a new agent or editing an existing agent fails — the editor page does not load. Screenshot upload failed, indicating a JavaScript error during agent editor initialization in 1.14.0.

source_issues.title: Unable to configure the addition of 'OAuth' for Notion data source
source_issues.evidence: When configuring Notion OAuth, clicking anywhere in the OAuth configuration popup causes it to immediately dismiss. Users cannot input credentials or complete OAuth setup. Clicking any element in the popup triggers dismissal.

signals.topic: Workflow API file upload broken in v1.14.0 — POST /v1/workflows/run with file inputs always returns 400 invalid_param
signals.summary: The API endpoint /v1/workflows/run rejects valid file_id inputs with a 400 error, making workflow automation via API impossible. Regression introduced in v1.14.0.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：API文件上传是自动化集成的核心路径。/v1/workflows/run是用户通过外部系统调用Dify工作流的主要方式。文件上传失败意味着所有依赖文件输入的工作流自动化场景完全不可用。复现路径清晰（上传文件→传file_id→调用workflow→400），v1.14.0引入（v1.13.0正常），属于明确的版本退化。

source_issues.title: [1.14.0] API file upload is broken, works fine in 1.13.0
source_issues.evidence: POST /v1/workflows/run with valid file_id returns 400 {code: invalid_param, message: Invalid upload file}. Affects all file input types (document, image). Both object and string format fail. Reproduction: upload file via /v1/files/upload, then pass file_id to workflow run — 400 error. Worked in 1.13.0.

signals.topic: Console GET /account/avatar endpoint has IDOR — any authenticated user can obtain signed download URLs for other users' upload files
signals.summary: The avatar endpoint does not verify that the requesting user owns the specified file ID, allowing any authenticated console user to access arbitrary file URLs belonging to other users in the same workspace.
signals.review_reason: 安全越权：任意认证用户可以通过猜测文件UUID获取同workspace内其他用户上传文件的签名下载地址。这是一个真实的未授权访问漏洞，不仅仅是安全关键词。漏洞已被安全研究者识别且有清晰的复现路径，展示了认证用户之间的文件访问隔离完全缺失。

source_issues.title: Console GET /account/avatar signs arbitrary upload file IDs without ownership checks (IDOR)
source_issues.evidence: Any authenticated console user B can call GET /console/api/account/avatar?avatar=<FILE_ID_FROM_USER_A> and receive a signed URL for user A's file. No tenant_id, created_by, or created_by_role check is performed. Exposes all upload files to any authenticated workspace member.

signals.topic: ExecutionContext.enter() leaks thread-local contextvars between request handlers — state from one request bleeds into subsequent requests on the same worker thread
signals.summary: ExecutionContext.enter() calls ContextVar.set() but never stores the returned Token or calls ContextVar.reset(token) on exit, causing the OS thread to retain the last set values after exiting the context manager. This means context isolation between workflow node executions on the same worker thread is broken.
signals.review_reason: 状态泄露：contextvars未正确重置导致同一worker线程上不同请求/节点之间的上下文状态互相污染。在多租户部署中，这可能导致应用A的上下文泄露到应用B的执行中，属于数据隔离层面的严重缺陷。代码层面有明确bug（set后未reset），且影响每个工作流节点执行路径。

source_issues.title: ExecutionContext.enter() sets contextvars but never resets tokens, leaking thread-local context between exits
source_issues.evidence: ExecutionContext.enter() calls var.set(val) without storing the Token returned by set(). When exiting the @contextmanager, ContextVar.reset(token) is never called. Every workflow node is wrapped in 'with self._execution_context:', so the thread's ContextVar values are not restored after each node. State from one node/request can bleed into the next on the same OS thread.

signals.topic: Embedding model connection via LiteLLM OpenAI-compatible provider fails with 422 — Dify sends encoding_format=null which LiteLLM rejects
signals.summary: When connecting an embedding model served via LiteLLM through Dify's OpenAI-compatible provider, Dify explicitly sets encoding_format to null, but LiteLLM only accepts 'float' or 'base64', causing a 422 validation error.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Embedding模型是RAG（检索增强生成）的核心组件。通过LiteLLM使用embedding模型的用户无法完成模型配置，导致RAG功能完全不可用。这是一个明确的集成失败，有完整的错误信息和根因（encoding_format=null vs litellm只接受float/base64）。

source_issues.title: 422 error when connection embedding model served via Litellm by Openai compatible provider
source_issues.evidence: LiteLLM returns 422 error because Dify's OpenAI-compatible provider sets encoding_format to null explicitly. LiteLLM only accepts 'float' or 'base64'. Embedding model cannot be added to the model list. Error: {'detail': [{'type': 'literal_error', 'loc': ['body', 'encoding_format'], 'msg': "Input should be 'float' or 'base64'", 'input': None}]}

signals.topic: gpt-5.4-mini API parameter incompatibility blocks all add() and search() calls
signals.summary: mem0 Python SDK passes `max_tokens` to gpt-5.4-mini, which requires `max_completion_tokens`. All client.add() (memory extraction) and client.search() calls silently fail with a 400 BadRequest error.
aliases: GPT-5.4-mini API incompatibility blocks memory operations
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker: every add() and search() call fails silently for gpt-5.4-mini users. The error is a hard 400 rejection from the OpenAI API, which means memory extraction completely fails. Count=1 but review_reason provides explicit user impact evidence — all memory operations are blocked.

source_issues.title: bug: _get_common_params passes max_tokens to gpt-5.4-mini, which requires max_completion_tokens
source_issues.evidence: All client.add() (extraction) and client.search() calls fail for users running gpt-5.4-mini as the LLM provider. Memory extraction silently fails — no memories are stored. Error: BadRequestError 400 — 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model. Use 'max_completion_tokens' instead.

signals.topic: TypeScript SDK v3 silently camelizes user-defined metadata keys on read, breaking v2→v3 round-trip
signals.summary: The v3 TS SDK applies snake→camel key transformation recursively into the opaque `metadata` blob on read, silently corrupting user-defined snake_case keys. Code relying on `metadata.message_id` returns undefined after upgrading, with no error or warning.
aliases: TS SDK metadata key case transformation breaks round-trip
TypeScript SDK metadata snake_case corruption on read
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow data corruption issue with explicit multi-scenario user impact evidence. The SDK silently rewrites user-defined metadata keys on read, breaking backward compatibility with v2 SDK in a way that produces no errors — code just silently returns undefined. Three concrete downstream effects documented: indexer misclassification, keyword index fragmentation, and adapter failures. This blocks users upgrading from v2 SDK.

source_issues.title: [TypeScript SDK] v3 silently camelizes user-defined `metadata` keys on read, breaking round-trip
source_issues.evidence: User documents three concrete real-world impacts: (1) an indexer silently classifying every memory as invalid because it filters by metadata.database_name (now databaseName), (2) keyword-search index fragmented with mixed snake/camel paths, (3) adapters reading metadata.message_id/supplier_id returning undefined for newly written memories. This is a silent breaking change from v2 SDK behavior.

signals.topic: OpenClaw integration: agent memory isolation, run_id, and autoCapture broken after OpenClaw 4.26+
signals.summary: After upgrading @mem0/openclaw-mem0 to v1.0.11 on OpenClaw 4.26+, agent-level memory isolation is broken (user_id not concatenated with agent suffix), run_id is always None preventing session filtering, and autoCapture fails to save memories. Root cause is register() being called multiple times per conversation with separate closures.
aliases: openclaw-mem0 agent isolation broken after OpenClaw upgrade
run_id always None in openclaw-mem0 integration
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core functionality of the openclaw-mem0 integration for users on OpenClaw 4.26+. Agent memory isolation, session filtering via run_id, and auto-capture are all broken — three separate ways the main memory workflow is blocked. Affects a specific integration (OpenClaw) rather than the core SDK.

source_issues.title: [openclaw-mem0] Agent isolation & run_id broken after OpenClaw 4.26+ upgrade
source_issues.evidence: Three distinct failures in the OpenClaw integration: (1) agent-level memory isolation broken — user_id not concatenated with agent suffix, (2) run_id always None — cannot filter memories by session, (3) autoCapture broken — memories not auto-saved after conversations. All are main flow failures for openclaw-mem0 users.

signals.topic: Entity store delete/update triggers O(n) full table scan, causing severe performance degradation at scale
signals.summary: _remove_memory_from_entity_store calls entity_store.list with top_k=10000 on every memory delete or update, fetching all entity rows including embedding vectors and scanning in Python. This is very slow and incomplete for stores with >10K vectors. A targeted jsonb containment query would be ~40x faster.
aliases: full table scan on memory delete/update
O(n) entity store lookup blocks delete/update operations
signals.review_reason: Significant performance degradation for a core operation (delete/update) that scales with data size. Every delete/update becomes O(n) full scan, which will eventually make memory management operations prohibitively slow as the store grows. Count=1 but 9 comments indicate community interest, and the 40x improvement claim provides concrete impact evidence.

source_issues.title: bug: avoid full table scan on every delete/update in _remove_memory_from_entity_store
source_issues.evidence: Performance issue explicitly described: O(n) full table scan on every memory delete or update. User reports this is 'very slow' and 'incomplete when the store is >10K vectors'. User provides measured evidence: ~40x performance improvement possible with targeted query. Affects all delete/update operations.

signals.topic: MemoryGraph structuredLlm hardcoded to openai_structured, blocking non-OpenAI providers from graph memory
signals.summary: When configuring mem0 OSS with a non-OpenAI LLM provider (Groq, Anthropic, etc.) for graph memory, MemoryGraph hardcodes structuredLlm to use 'openai_structured' while passing the main LLM's config containing the non-OpenAI API key. This causes 401 authentication errors, completely blocking graph memory usage for all non-OpenAI users.
aliases: non-OpenAI providers cannot use graph memory due to hardcoded openai_structured LLM
Graph memory 401 auth error with non-OpenAI LLM providers
signals.review_reason: Hard block for a significant user segment (anyone using non-OpenAI LLM providers). Graph memory is completely unusable with Groq, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, etc. due to a hardcoded provider. This forces users to either use OpenAI (losing cost/speed benefits of alternatives) or abandon graph memory entirely.

source_issues.title: Bug: MemoryGraph.structuredLlm hardcoded to openai_structured prevents use of non-OpenAI providers
source_issues.evidence: Hard block: 'Completely blocks usage of mem0 graph memory with non-OpenAI providers.' Error: AuthenticationError 401 — using Groq API key against OpenAI API. Users of Groq (9x faster), Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, and other non-OpenAI providers cannot use graph memory at all. Workaround forces OpenAI provider usage.

signals.topic: Approval-required tool flow causes HTTP 400 errors across multiple .NET code paths (externalLoop + ApprovalRequiredAIFunction, GroupChat)
signals.summary: When a workflow uses a tool wrapped in ApprovalRequiredAIFunction or HITL approval, the second turn fails with HTTP 400: 'No tool output found for function call' (externalLoop path) or 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceding message with tool_calls' (GroupChat path). This blocks the canonical human-in-the-loop approval pattern in production declarative workflows and multi-agent GroupChat scenarios.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct issues (2 .NET code paths + 1 Python path) all manifest as HTTP 400 errors when the workflow attempts to continue after a human approves a tool. Each issue has a clear error message and blocks the canonical human-in-the-loop approval pattern — a production-critical feature. Count=3 meets the P0 frequency threshold.

source_issues.title: .NET: `externalLoop` + `ApprovalRequiredAIFunction` leaves dangling `function_call` in Azure Conversations API, breaks resume
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 400: No tool output found for function call on second turn after client posts mcp_approval_response. Blocks canonical pattern of 'agent with a tool that requires approval' inside declarative workflow on Foundry hosting.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: GroupChat tool approval flow causes HTTP 400 — tool message without preceding assistant tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: After tool approval executes in GroupChatBuilder, workflow crashes with HTTP 400: 'messages with role tool must be a response to a preceding message with tool_calls'. Conversation history is missing the assistant message containing original tool_calls.

source_issues.title: Python: Hosted Agent Framework: human-in-the-loop tool approval not working
source_issues.evidence: When using @tool(approval_mode='always_require') in hosted Agent Framework, shows warning 'Content type function_approval_request is not supported yet'. Human-in-the-loop approval flow does not work in hosted scenario.

signals.topic: MultiPartyConversation._history silently dropped during SerializeSessionAsync → DeserializeSessionAsync round-trip, causing 'Bookmark value too large' errors
signals.summary: _history field in MultiPartyConversation has no public accessor and no [JsonInclude] attribute, so System.Text.Json silently drops it during STJ serialization. On the next turn, the conversation resumes with an empty history, causing 'Bookmark value too large' errors that block session resumption in .NET 1.3.
aliases: Bookmark value too large on session resume
signals.review_reason: Session resumption is a core functional requirement. The bug is insidious — STJ silently drops a field with no warning, only surfacing as a confusing 'Bookmark value too large' error on the next turn. This directly breaks multi-turn conversation continuity, a key agent framework use case. count=1 but severity is high (hidden data loss during serialization).

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: MultiPartyConversation._history is dropped during workflow-as-agent session round-trip → Bookmark value too large on next turn (1.3)
source_issues.evidence: _history has no public accessor and no [JsonInclude], so STJ silently drops it during serialization. After DeserializeSessionAsync, history is gone. On next turn: 'Bookmark value too large' error. Root cause is a hidden implementation detail that only surfaces as a runtime failure.

signals.topic: agent-framework-foundry v1.2.2 cannot import AgentMiddlewareLayer from agent-framework v1.2.2 due to missing __init__.py export
signals.summary: agent-framework-foundry v1.2.2 raises ImportError when importing AgentMiddlewareLayer from agent-framework v1.2.2. The class exists in agent_framework._middleware but is not re-exported from the package __init__.py, making the entire agent-framework-foundry integration unusable for v1.2.2 users.
signals.review_reason: ImportError is a complete blocker — no user code can run when the top-level import fails. This is not a cosmetic issue; it makes the entire agent-framework-foundry integration dead on arrival for v1.2.2. Confirmed by two packages at the same version, pointing to a packaging regression.

source_issues.title: Python: ImportError: agent-framework-foundry 1.2.2 cannot import AgentMiddlewareLayer from agent-framework 1.2.2
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: agent-framework-foundry v1.2.2 cannot import AgentMiddlewareLayer from agent-framework v1.2.2. Class exists in agent_framework._middleware but is not re-exported from __init__.py. Makes entire agent-framework-foundry integration unusable.

signals.topic: HostedImageGenerationTool throws NullReferenceException when output file format value is null, crashing image generation
signals.summary: NullReferenceException thrown at ImageGenerationToolOutputFileFormat..ctor when the value parameter is null. This crashes the entire hosted image generation flow whenever a null output format is encountered, making the HostedImageGenerationTool unreliable in production.
signals.review_reason: NullReferenceException is an unhandled crash that completely kills the image generation workflow. Unlike a graceful error, this is an unhandled exception that propagates up and stops execution. Labeled as bug with clear stack trace location. count=1 but unhandled NRE warrants P1.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: HostedImageGenerationTool throws NullReferenceException
source_issues.evidence: NullReferenceException at ImageGenerationToolOutputFileFormat..ctor when value is null. Directly crashes the hosted image generation workflow. Labeled as bug.

signals.topic: Magentic orchestration stops after first query completion, breaking multi-query conversation flows
signals.summary: When using Magentic (a Microsoft-provided orchestration integration), the workflow stops after the first query completes and does not progress to subsequent queries. Expected behavior is automatic continuation through all queries in a multi-turn conversation. This blocks the primary multi-query use case for Magentic users.
aliases: multi-query conversation stops after first query
signals.review_reason: Multi-query conversation flows are a core orchestration scenario. Early termination after the first query breaks the expected sequential query pattern. However, Magentic is an external integration (not core framework), and count=1 reduces confidence. Kept with P2 as it still represents a real user experience failure for affected users.

source_issues.title: Magentic orchestration stops after first query completion and does not continue to the next query
source_issues.evidence: Magentic orchestration stops after first query completes and does not continue to next query. User expects automatic progression to subsequent queries in a multi-turn conversation. Labels include 'agent orchestration' and 'workflows'.

signals.topic: Multi-agent loop termination behavior is non-deterministic, causing reproducibility and safety validation issues
signals.summary: Termination behavior in multi-agent loops varies with timing and tool-response ordering, leading to non-deterministic step counts and termination reasons. This blocks reproducibility and makes safety guarantees hard to validate in autonomous loops.
signals.review_reason: Non-deterministic termination in multi-agent loops is a real user-impacting issue that affects reproducibility and safety validation of autonomous agent workflows. While count=1, the severity is high — it undermines the reliability of autonomous loops, a core use case of AutoGen.

source_issues.title: Add deterministic termination contract tests for multi-agent loops
source_issues.evidence: User reports equivalent loop fixtures produce varying termination reasons and step counts across repeated runs. macOS Darwin 25.3.0 arm64, Python 3.14.0. Affects autonomous multi-agent loops where safety guarantees cannot be reliably validated.

signals.topic: Cannot consume OpenAI API via custom HTTP endpoint — library only supports direct library calls
signals.summary: Users cannot route OpenAI API calls through a custom intermediate endpoint. The autogen library implementation only supports direct calls using the official OpenAI library, blocking the ability to use custom proxy/gateway endpoints.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete functional limitation — users cannot route OpenAI API calls through custom intermediate endpoints (e.g., proxies, gateways). This blocks enterprise/infrastructure use cases where routing through a custom endpoint is required. The issue has been open since 2025-05-15 with 9 comments, indicating ongoing user demand.

source_issues.title: cant consume openai via requests
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states they need to consume OpenAI via a custom intermediate endpoint (not direct library calls). Current implementation only supports direct calls. This is a functional limitation blocking a real use case.

signals.topic: MCP browser in headed mode uses chromeless app mode and tears down between tool calls
signals.summary: Since @playwright/mcp 0.0.73, headed browser sessions are incorrectly routed through launchApp which applies --app=chromeless flags, stripping toolbar/address bar. The browser context is also torn down between MCP tool calls, making headed mode unusable for AI agent workflows.
signals.review_reason: MCP headed mode is completely broken in 0.0.73 (regression from 0.0.72). Browser is chromeless and tears down between calls, making any AI agent workflow using headed browsers impossible. Clear user impact with identified root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug] @playwright/mcp 0.0.73 routes headed browser through launchApp — chromeless --app= window, dies between tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in launchApp.ts: --app=data:text/html, is unconditionally pushed, stripping browser chrome. Browser then tears down after each MCP call, so subsequent calls fail with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. Regression from 0.0.72. Reporter and another user affected.

signals.topic: Firefox: pointer events fail in parallel test execution
signals.summary: When running Playwright tests in parallel on Firefox, pointer events (hover, click) only work in 1 out of N pages. The same tests pass in serial mode or on Chromium/Safari. Affects any user running parallel E2E tests on Firefox.
signals.review_reason: Parallel test execution is a core Playwright use case. Firefox is a Tier-1 browser target. When tests run in parallel, pointer events silently fail on all but one page, making test suites unreliable on Firefox. This is a persistent regression affecting a Tier-1 browser in a fundamental workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Pointer events don't work in Firefox in parallel
source_issues.evidence: Repro shows 5 pages with Promise.all hover/tooltip checks fail on Firefox only in parallel mode; same code works in series. Labeled P3 by maintainers. Previously reported in #27517 (closed for bandwidth 2 years ago). Reproduces in both headed and headless modes.

signals.topic: Full-page screenshot does not render iframe content, shows blank white area
signals.summary: When taking a full-page screenshot that includes iframes (e.g. YouTube embeds), the iframe area renders as blank white instead of the actual iframe content. Users relying on full-page screenshots for visual regression testing or documentation get incorrect output.
signals.review_reason: Full-page screenshot is a core feature used for visual regression testing and documentation. When iframes render as blank white, the screenshot is silently incorrect — users may not notice and make wrong assertions. Clear functional regression in screenshot rendering.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Full-page screenshot doesn't render iframe content
source_issues.evidence: Repro repo provided with YouTube iframe test. full-page.png shows iframe area as blank white; viewport and iframe-element screenshots render correctly. Labeled P3 by maintainers, indicating known issue.

signals.topic: MCP session isolation missing: multiple AI agents cannot share MCP server concurrently
signals.summary: The MCP server uses a single browser session, causing profile lock contention when multiple AI agents try to use Playwright MCP simultaneously. Each new session closes the previous one, blocking parallel AI agent workflows.
signals.review_reason: Multiple AI agents sharing a single MCP server cannot work concurrently due to single-session design. The feature request comes from the MCP package maintainer and directly references a confirmed parallel client issue in playwright-mcp. This blocks a primary use case (AI agent orchestration).

source_issues.title: feat(mcp): add sessionId parameter for multi-session browser isolation
source_issues.evidence: Feature request from MCP maintainer. Currently each MCP connection gets exactly one browser instance. Multiple MCP clients in the same workspace cannot use browser simultaneously — only one session at a time. Related microsoft/playwright-mcp#1594 confirms profile lock with multiple clients. Blocks advanced AI agent multi-account/multi-site workflows.

signals.topic: ElectronApplication.close() hangs indefinitely on unclean shutdown
signals.summary: electronApp.close() waits forever if Electron has before-quit handlers, leaky IPC handlers, or child processes that prevent exit. Users are forced to build multi-layer timeout workarounds. Multiple linked issues confirm widespread occurrence.
signals.review_reason: electronApp.close() hanging blocks automated test teardown in CI, causing cascading failures. Four linked issues across years confirm this is a recurring, widespread problem for Electron users. The test-level timeout workaround is poor UX and wastes CI time.

source_issues.title: feat(electron): add timeout option to electronApp.close() for force-kill escalation
source_issues.evidence: Feature request cites 4 linked issues (#12189, #27523, #39248, #13874) all about Electron close() hanging. Reporter maintains E2E tests for VS Code extension and had to build 3-layer workaround. The hang blocks test teardown, causing cascading failures in CI.

signals.topic: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync fails with NOT NULL constraint violation on words.json column
signals.summary: When calling UpsertAsync on a SqliteVectorStore collection, SQLite throws 'NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json' because the connector serializes non-vector properties into null/empty values, violating the NOT NULL schema constraint. Workarounds fail and only raw SQL bypasses the bug.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine workflow_runtime pain point. The SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync operation fails unconditionally with a NOT NULL constraint violation. Users cannot use the official connector for the primary upsert workflow — only a raw SQL workaround succeeds. This blocks the core use case of storing vectorized data in SQLite.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: [SqliteVectorStore] NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json during UpsertAsync
source_issues.evidence: UpsertAsync (single or batch) throws 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json'. The json column is defined as NOT NULL but the connector serializes non-vector properties into null/empty value, violating the constraint. Workarounds tried (explicit non-empty values, relaxed schema) all fail. Only raw SQL bypasses the bug. User's entire use case (vector store upsert) is completely blocked.

signals.topic: Usage quota display incorrectly shows 100% / full with no actual usage; weekly reset shows phantom usage
signals.summary: Weekly usage display shows 100%/full consumption even when the user has not used Codex, with renewal date jumping forward. Users return to find their remaining quota missing without any corresponding activity.
aliases: credits not reflected in usage popup
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports of quota metering/display bugs causing paid quota to appear unavailable. Issue #21226 shows phantom usage that consumed 30% of quota without any activity (direct cost loss). Issue #21240 shows purchased credits not reflected in the usage display. Both create a situation where users believe they cannot use Codex despite having legitimate quota.

source_issues.title: Weekly Limit Increased to 100% Without Any Usage
source_issues.evidence: User reports weekly usage jumped from 70% to 100% with renewal date shifting from May 7 to May 12, despite zero usage over 2 days. 30% of quota disappeared without corresponding activity. Direct cost impact: user cannot access quota they paid for.

source_issues.title: Usage popup even after adding credits
source_issues.evidence: User purchased Codex credits, restarted the app, and the usage limit popup still appeared despite having 'plenty of credits remaining.' The popup incorrectly implies the user has no quota available when they do.

signals.topic: /copy copies only the last assistant step instead of the full multi-step response
signals.summary: When Codex outputs a multi-step response, the /copy command and Ctrl-O shortcut only copy the last step, omitting earlier steps (explanation, diff, notes). Users lose important content like exact diffs.
signals.review_reason: User-impacting bug: key content (diffs, explanations) is silently dropped from clipboard when using /copy, directly reducing the utility of the feature. Users rely on /copy to extract Codex output; losing the full response forces manual copy workarounds.

source_issues.title: /copy only copies the latest assistant step instead of the full multi-step response
source_issues.evidence: User reports that /copy and Ctrl-O only copy the last assistant step, losing earlier steps containing diffs, explanations, and notes. The UI presents multi-step output as one response but the clipboard only receives the last fragment.

signals.topic: Codex CLI hangs indefinitely on every prompt (no response, no error)
signals.summary: The codex-cli becomes unresponsive on every prompt, providing no response and no error message. Users cannot complete any workflow.
signals.review_reason: P0: Main CLI workflow is completely blocked. Every single user prompt hangs with no response, meaning the primary interaction loop of the Codex CLI is entirely non-functional. No workaround available.

source_issues.title: codex-cli stucks on every prompt
source_issues.evidence: User on WSL/Linux reports codex-cli hangs on every prompt with no response or error. Main CLI workflow is completely blocked for this user.

signals.topic: Codex CLI /review ignores local-only restriction and invokes GitHub MCP tools
signals.summary: The /review slash command calls GitHub MCP connector tools even when the user explicitly prohibits GitHub MCP tools and requests local-only review.
signals.review_reason: Trust/privacy violation: /review bypasses an explicit user constraint (no GitHub MCP tools) and silently accesses connected GitHub integrations. The model is actively violating a user-specified operational constraint, which is a meaningful trust regression.

source_issues.title: /review invokes GitHub MCP tools despite explicit local-only restriction
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly prohibited GitHub MCP tools. Despite this, /review attempted to use GitHub MCP tooling (codex_apps.github_list_repositories). This is a behavior regression. Creates trust and privacy issue: local-only operation expectation violated.

signals.topic: Codex CLI / native runtime grows unbounded and is OOM-killed by Linux kernel during short sessions
signals.summary: The codex-cli native/runtime process grows without bound during implementation sessions on large repos (~1.2GB), consuming up to 29GB RSS before being killed by the Linux cgroup OOM killer, even in sessions under 10 minutes.
signals.review_reason: P1 (count=1): Severe work-session blocking with very strong evidence (kernel logs, multiple version reproduction). Sessions under 10 minutes are terminated by the kernel OOM killer, causing total work loss. Count=1 means P0 threshold not met, but the severity and evidence quality are exceptional. Workaround (cgroup caps) does not prevent failure — only limits the damage.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI/native runtime grows to unbounded size and is killed by Linux cgroup OOM even during short implementation sessions
source_issues.evidence: User provides kernel logs showing 'Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process MainThread' at 18.7GB and 29.2GB RSS. Process named MainThread/tokio-runtime-w. Reproduced across v0.128.0, v0.124.0, v0.120.0. Work session fails catastrophically — process is kernel-killed, losing all progress.

signals.topic: Session history silently lost during multi-turn conversations (OpenAIConversationsSession & OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession)
signals.summary: OpenAIConversationsSession drops prior assistant messages after N turns on gpt-5.4/5.5 (producing [u,u,u,u,a] instead of [u,a,u,a,u,a]). OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession can permanently delete session history when run_compaction() clears then fails to write replacement items. rewind_session_items() can delete unrelated tail items during retry cleanup.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed session data loss bugs across 3 different session implementations. All produce silent/permanent data loss with no error surfaced to the user — violating the SDK's documented contract that Sessions maintain conversation history. #3123 explicitly breaks the multi-turn context contract on newer models. #3116 causes permanent history deletion on compaction failure. #3089 deletes unrelated session items during retry. Count=3 meets P0 threshold.

source_issues.title: OpenAIConversationsSession loses prior assistant items
source_issues.evidence: Silent data loss: session.get_items() drops prior assistant messages on gpt-5.4/5.5 with no error raised. Conversation shaped [u,u,u,u,a] instead of [u,a,u,a,u,a]. Response objects still exist on platform dashboard — SDK silently unlinks them.

source_issues.title: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession can lose session history if add_items fails after clear
source_issues.evidence: Permanent data loss: run_compaction() clears the underlying session then fails while writing compacted replacement items. No atomic replacement or clear-then-add failure recovery. Related prior PRs (#2317, #2322, #2333, #2334, #2343, #2344) addressed related issues but not this specific failure mode.

source_issues.title: rewind_session_items can delete unrelated tail session items during retry cleanup
source_issues.evidence: Silent data loss: rewind_session_items() pops items before confirming the session tail matches the target suffix, and in server_tracker cleanup keeps popping until finding a known server item — deleting unrelated new items that did not belong to the retry being rolled back.

signals.topic: Function tool executes despite is_enabled=False (dynamic tool disabling broken)
signals.summary: A function tool visible to the model, then dynamically disabled via is_enabled returning False before execution, still executes — violating the is_enabled contract.
aliases: tool remains enabled after dynamic disabling
signals.review_reason: Single issue but represents a core SDK contract violation: is_enabled returning False should prevent execution, but it does not. This is a bypassable safety mechanism affecting any agent using dynamic tool gating. Not P0 because count=1 and the exact failure path (tool visibility vs execution gating) is not fully detailed in the report.

source_issues.title: Dynamic function tool is still executed after is_enabled becomes false
source_issues.evidence: Tool visibility and execution are not separated: once a tool is shown to the model, disabling it via is_enabled before execution does not prevent execution. This breaks a core safety/control mechanism users rely on for dynamic tool gating.

signals.topic: Tracing privacy setting trace_include_sensitive_data=False is bypassed by function tool error paths
signals.summary: Function tool failures attach raw error strings (potentially containing sensitive data) to trace spans even when RunConfig(trace_include_sensitive_data=False) is set. Other tool execution paths (computer, shell) already use a redacting helper, but function tool paths do not.
aliases: sensitive data leakage in traces despite privacy config
trace_include_sensitive_data ignored in tool error handling
signals.review_reason: Users explicitly configuring trace_include_sensitive_data=False expect no sensitive data in traces. The function tool error path leaks raw error strings regardless, while the codebase already has a redaction helper for other tool paths. This is a privacy/data exposure issue with clear user intent violation.

source_issues.title: Function tool trace errors ignore trace_include_sensitive_data=False
source_issues.evidence: RunConfig(trace_include_sensitive_data=False) is explicitly set by users to prevent sensitive data from appearing in traces. The function tool error path in _run_single_tool() calls attach_error_to_current_span() with str(e) directly, bypassing the redaction helper that other tool paths already use.

signals.topic: Responses API streaming treats failed and incomplete terminal events as success
signals.summary: stream_response() and websocket get_response() in the Responses streaming path accept response.failed and response.incomplete as valid final responses. This allows a run to finish with apparent success even though the Responses API reported a terminal failure.
aliases: streaming masks API failures as success
failed/incomplete response treated as valid output
signals.review_reason: Streaming path silently masks terminal API failures as success. Users receive no error signal when the Responses API has explicitly terminated with failure/incomplete. This is a silent workflow failure — the run completes without error but the response content is from a failed API call. High impact but count=1 so P1.

source_issues.title: Responses streaming treats failed and incomplete terminal events as success
source_issues.evidence: stream_response() stores response.failed and response.incomplete payloads as final_response. The streamed runner finalization converts them into ModelResponse as if successful. Users see no error while the API has signaled a terminal failure, causing silent data loss and incorrect run completion.

signals.topic: Workspace hydrate tarfile extraction accepts symlink targets outside archive root (path traversal)
signals.summary: validate_tarfile() validates member paths but not symlink linknames. Hydrate/restore flows that intentionally allow symlinks will accept entries whose targets point outside the extracted archive root (e.g., ../../outside, /etc/passwd).
aliases: symlink path traversal in tarfile extraction
signals.review_reason: Path traversal vulnerability in workspace hydrate flow. Malicious tar archives with symlinks pointing outside the extraction root can write arbitrary files. Affects sandbox session restore/hydrate flows. Security impact but scoped to a specific code path (allow_symlinks=True flows only).

source_issues.title: workspace hydrate accepts symlink targets outside the archive root
source_issues.evidence: UnixLocalSandboxSession.hydrate_workspace() and DockerSandboxSession.hydrate_workspace() call safe_extract_tarfile() which validates tar member paths but not symlink linknames. Allows arbitrary file writes outside archive root via malicious symlinks. Regular extract() uses allow_symlinks=False so this is specific to hydrate/restore flows.

signals.topic: Responses stream accumulator crashes with AttributeError when event.item is None on response.output_item.added
signals.summary: When using OpenAI-compatible custom providers that emit response.output_item.added with item=null, the Responses stream accumulator dereferences event.item.type without null check, causing AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type'. This hard-crashes the SDK stream before application code can recover.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking crash: the SDK stream accumulator hard-crashes with AttributeError when any compatible provider emits response.output_item.added with item=None. The crash occurs inside the SDK before any application-level error handling can catch it, completely blocking streaming workflows. Severity is amplified because it affects custom providers (not just OpenAI's own API), making it a widespread risk for anyone using OpenAI-compatible backends.

source_issues.title: Responses stream accumulator crashes when response.output_item.added has item=None
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type' thrown inside SDK stream accumulator on response.output_item.added with item=None. Affects any OpenAI-compatible custom provider emitting the malformed event. No recovery possible from application code since crash occurs inside SDK.

signals.topic: Async Responses parse() causes unbounded memory leak from Pydantic TypeVar schema rebuilds
signals.summary: AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models causes unbounded memory growth. ParsedResponse[TextFormatT] uses an unresolved TypeVar, causing pydantic model_rebuild() to always fail, meaning a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust object) is allocated on every single parse() call. In long-running servers this leads to linear RSS growth and eventual OOM crash.
aliases: OOM from unbounded pydantic schema rebuild
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking memory leak causing eventual OOM crash in long-running servers. A flame graph is provided as evidence. The root cause is precisely identified: unresolved TypeVar prevents pydantic caching, causing unbounded SchemaValidator allocations on every parse() call. This is not an edge case—it affects every user of AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models, making it a critical reliability issue.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Flame graph evidence provided showing memory leak. Root cause identified: TextFormatT TypeVar prevents pydantic model_rebuild cache from being populated. Each parse() call allocates a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust object) that accumulates without bound. Long-running server with repeated parse() calls will grow RSS linearly and eventually OOM.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely when file status stuck at in_progress
signals.summary: upload_and_poll() has no timeout and no error terminal state. When the vector store file processing/indexing stalls (file stays at status='in_progress' forever, last_error=null, raw file already='processed'), the function blocks indefinitely with no way to recover or detect the failure.
aliases: vector store file processing stuck in_progress
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking hang: upload_and_poll() has no timeout and no terminal error state, causing indefinite blocking when file processing stalls. The function is completely unusable in this failure mode—no error is raised, no return value, no timeout exception. This blocks any pipeline relying on vector store file availability and the user has no workaround within the SDK.

source_issues.title: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at in_progress
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely when vector store file processing stalls. File stays at status='in_progress' forever with last_error=null while raw file is already 'processed'. The function has no timeout mechanism and no way to detect terminal failure, completely blocking any workflow relying on vector store file availability.

signals.topic: ResponseFunctionWebSearch type definition allows action=None at runtime but type annotation forbids it, causing AttributeError in user code
signals.summary: The ResponseFunctionWebSearch type does not indicate that action can be None, but the API returns action=None for some web search calls. User code that safely assumes action.type=='search' (consistent with the type definition) crashes at runtime with AttributeError when action is None. This is a type definition gap causing production crashes.
signals.review_reason: This is a type definition gap that causes production runtime crashes: the type says action cannot be None but the API returns action=None for some web search calls. User code written to match the type contract crashes at runtime. This is not a minor type-hint inconvenience—it causes real crashes in production when iterating over web search output. The workaround (adding null checks) requires users to discover the gap empirically, which is a poor developer experience.

source_issues.title: ResponseFunctionWebSearch doesn't match returned payload
source_issues.evidence: ResponseFunctionWebSearch(action=None) is returned by the API but the type annotation implies action cannot be None. Code that assumes action.type=='search' (based on the types) crashes with AttributeError when action is None. User had to add null-checks as a workaround after discovering the mismatch in production.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD causing intermittent deserialization failures
signals.summary: In multiprocess forkserver environments (common for high-throughput serving), openai SDK with pydantic 2.12 raises intermittent PydanticUserError during deserialization. With DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true: ~0.6% error rate growing over time (millions of requests). With DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false: ~9.5% error rate. The hardcoded _parent_namespace_depth=5 in pydantic's model_rebuild fails silently in fork worker processes.
signals.review_reason: This causes significant production errors in high-throughput serving environments using multiprocess forkserver (a common production pattern). Error rates of 0.6-9.5% mean thousands of failed requests per million in production. The failure is non-deterministic (depends on fork timing) making it hard to debug. The root cause is a pydantic namespace resolution issue triggered by the forkserver pattern, which is a legitimate production deployment concern.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: In production forkserver environment with ~700 workers processing millions of requests: ~0.6% error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true, growing over time. ~9.5% error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false where eager build fails at import time for ~9.5% of workers, causing ALL requests for those workers to fail. Root cause: _parent_namespace_depth=5 walks call stack and fails silently in fork workers.

signals.topic: Spec defines constraints or prohibitions without executable fallback paths — agents forced to violate rules or abandon tasks when primary methods fail
signals.summary: Multiple skill specs state requirements or prohibitions (never write .safe files, use dedicated wallet, prohibit --break-system-packages) without defining what the agent should do when those constraints cannot be satisfied. Agents either violate the prohibition or stop entirely, leaving user tasks unfulfilled.
aliases: Spec prohibits tool's standard interface without showing pipe alternative
Spec prohibition without viable fallback forces agent to violate rule
Spec references non-existent allowlist/script causing agent to auto-create unreviewed code
Spec approval flow not mapped to executable commands
Wallet policy declared without verification procedure
signals.review_reason: Five skills exhibit variants of the same systemic failure: the spec defines a constraint or references a resource without providing the executable alternative or error-handling path. In #2019 the consequence is severe — the agent auto-generates security audit code that bypasses the spec's own verification mechanism. In #2027 the agent is forced to violate a prohibition because no viable path exists. These represent both workflow blocking and security boundary erosion.

source_issues.title: security: qr-code-generator skill spec Prohibits Fallback But All Approved Alternatives Fail in Agent Environment
source_issues.evidence: Spec prohibits --break-system-packages and suggests venv. Both pip install and python3 -m venv fail during execution. Agent is forced to either violate the prohibition or stop entirely. Spec never says 'if all options fail, stop' — so agent has no resolution path.

source_issues.title: security: Spec References Non-Existent Resources, Agent Auto-Creates and Bypasses Security Boundary
source_issues.evidence: macarena-test SKILL.md declares a verified mode with a command allowlist and collection script. Neither file exists in the skill package. Agent auto-creates its own versions from scratch — building and executing unreviewed security audit scripts that bypass the verification the spec was designed to enforce.

source_issues.title: Security: binance-dca-test — Missing Implementation + Incomplete Guardrails
source_issues.evidence: binance-dca-test SKILL.md describes scripts/dca.sh for executing DCA trades. The scripts/ directory and dca.sh do not exist in the package. The advertised CLI interface is unimplemented. Agent cannot complete the advertised financial-trading function.

source_issues.title: security: openclast-wallet Spec Defines Approval Flow But Doesn't Map It to Concrete Commands
source_issues.evidence: openclast-wallet spec defines a mandatory three-step approval flow (create pending, user approve, broadcast) but doesn't document which CLI commands correspond to each step. Agent understands the concept but guesses a command that doesn't exist in the spec.

source_issues.title: security: quickintel-scan skill Spec Declares Wallet Policy Without Defining Verification Procedure
source_issues.evidence: Spec says 'Only use a dedicated hot wallet with minimal funds ($1-5 USDC).' Agent reads process.env.X402_PRIVATE_KEY directly without any verification — no balance check, no user confirmation, no warning. No procedure defined for how the agent should validate the wallet constraint.

signals.topic: Spec self-contradiction drives agents to skip safety steps or execute dangerous commands — security notes contradict operational guidance across multiple skills
signals.summary: Multiple skill specs contain internal contradictions where security notes call an operation destructive or require review, while quick-start or body text labels the same operation 'safe' or routine. Agents follow the permissive text and skip safety steps, executing destructive commands without backup or review.
aliases: Spec contradiction between security notes and quick start
Safe installer label contradicts should-review note
Systemic spec contradiction on --yes destructive flags
signals.review_reason: This is a systemic design flaw, not an isolated incident. Four separate skills across different publishers exhibit the same pattern: spec self-contradiction between security guidance and operational text. In #2023 and #2017 the agent's behavior is explicitly documented (follows permissive text, skips safety step). The contradiction pattern forces agents to make unsafe choices regardless of intent.

source_issues.title: Security: skill specs Document --yes Flag Without Chat-Level Confirmation Replacement
source_issues.evidence: Systemic pattern: skill specs document CLI commands with --yes (skip confirmation) flags in examples. Agents must use --yes because CLI prompts would hang otherwise (no stdin in agent execution). But specs never require the agent to confirm with the user in chat before running --yes commands. Multiple skills affected.

source_issues.title: security: openfunderse-participant Spec's Security Notes Contradict Its Quick Start — Agent Follows Quick Start
source_issues.evidence: Spec has two sections for the same bot-init operation: Security Notes call it destructive requiring backup; Quick Start presents it as routine with --yes and no backup. Agent follows Quick Start and skips backup, as explicitly stated in the issue.

source_issues.title: Security: Spec's Contradictory "Safe Installer" Label vs "Should Review" Note Leads to Unreviewed `curl | bash`
source_issues.evidence: Spec metadata says 'review scripts before executing'; spec body calls the same curl|bash command 'The safe installer'. Agent trusts the 'safe' label and pipes remote script directly to bash without review, as explicitly described.

source_issues.title: Security: cf-manager Spec Defines Constraint Without Covering Failure Path
source_issues.evidence: User asks agent to write Cloudflare API token to config file. Agent correctly identifies security-sensitive operation but encounters permission denied when trying mkdir -p ~/.config/cloudflare. Spec defines the credential-storage constraint but provides no fallback path when permission errors occur. No resolution described.

signals.topic: Missing confirmation guardrails on high-stakes operations — financial trades and destructive actions execute without user approval
signals.summary: Multiple skills performing financial transactions (real Binance market orders) or destructive actions (sending mail) lack any guardrail requiring user confirmation before execution. When an agent uses these skills, real monetary losses or unintended communications can result.
aliases: Financial trading skill has no trade confirmation
Vague confirmation guardrail allows mail send after user refusal
signals.review_reason: These are not speculative risks — they represent known architectural gaps where high-stakes operations (real money trading, email sending) have no user-confirmation mechanism in the spec. #2031 is the highest-impact case: a DCA trading skill placing real market orders with no confirmation gate. #2018 shows actual harm: agent sent mail after user refused, demonstrating the vague guardrail failed to prevent the action.

source_issues.title: security: skill binance-dca-tool skip Has No Confirmation Guardrail
source_issues.evidence: binance-dca-tool executes real market buy orders on Binance. Spec's only guardrails are about credential storage (never hardcode, use env vars). There is zero guardrail requiring user confirmation before placing a trade. If agent uses this skill, real money is at risk with no user approval step.

source_issues.title: Security: Skill gog -- One-Sentence Guardrail Too Vague to Enforce Confirmation
source_issues.evidence: gog skill's only guardrail is six words: 'Confirm before sending mail or creating events.' Every dimension is undefined — what counts as confirmation, what form it takes, what to do if user changes mind. Agent executes gog gmail send after user explicitly refuses because nothing in spec tells it not to.

signals.topic: Vague confirmation language in skill specs fails to prevent unintended agent actions — single-sentence guardrails leave critical dimensions undefined
signals.summary: Skill specs use extremely brief confirmation directives (e.g., 'Confirm before sending mail') that leave every dimension undefined: what constitutes confirmation, who confirms, what form it takes, and what to do if the user refuses. Agents interpret the vague language in ways that contradict user intent.
aliases: One-sentence guardrail too vague to enforce
Temporal gap between verification and action in installation steps
signals.review_reason: Vague single-sentence guardrails are demonstrably ineffective. #2018 shows concrete harm: agent sent mail after user refused, proving the vague guardrail failed. #2014 shows the same pattern with npm install — the vague 'review before using' step was skipped because no one defined what it meant operationally. These are not theoretical: the vague language enables agents to rationalize proceeding against user intent.

source_issues.title: Security: Skill gog -- One-Sentence Guardrail Too Vague to Enforce Confirmation
source_issues.evidence: gog skill's only guardrail is six words: 'Confirm before sending mail or creating events.' Agent executes gog gmail send after user explicitly refuses because nothing in spec defines what confirmation means, what form it takes, or what to do when user says no.

source_issues.title: Security:Skill entradex — Spec's Vague 'Before Using' Creates Temporal Gap Between Verification and Installation
source_issues.evidence: entradex spec says 'Before using, please review...' but never specifies who reviews, what specifically to review, or what constitutes passing the review. Agent installs npm package immediately (Turn 1) after user asks to install it (Turn 0) — the vague 'before using' step is skipped entirely.

signals.topic: Account lockout after GitHub OAuth account deletion — soft-delete leaves OAuth binding preventing re-login
signals.summary: Users whose GitHub accounts are deleted or locked cannot re-register or log in to ClawHub because the OAuth binding persists after account deletion (soft-delete bug). This completely blocks platform access.
aliases: GitHub OAuth lockout after account deletion
Cannot login after GitHub account deletion
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user-impact bug: the soft-delete implementation leaves GitHub OAuth bindings intact, making it impossible for users to re-register after their GitHub account is deleted or locked. Platform access is completely blocked. No mitigation path exists for affected users.

source_issues.title: Cannot login after account deletion (GitHub OAuth locked)
source_issues.evidence: User reports their GitHub account is permanently locked after deletion, they cannot re-register or login, and attributes it to a soft-delete issue where the GitHub OAuth binding persists. Blocking platform access entirely.

signals.topic: WSL gateway onboarding validation blocks main setup flow with 8 distinct validation failures
signals.summary: WSL local gateway onboarding validation fails at multiple steps including settings isolation breach, stale executable launch, operator auth failure, token redaction gaps, wsl.conf probe weakness, docs/code mismatch, cancellation cleanup, and legacy token confusion — collectively blocking WSL gateway onboarding from completing.
signals.review_reason: Main onboarding flow is blocked end-to-end. The validation harness contaminated real user settings during WSL gateway setup (critical data-integrity issue), operator pairing fails with auth rejection preventing setup completion, and there are 6 additional co-occurring validation failures. This is a high-impact blocking issue for any user attempting WSL local gateway onboarding.

source_issues.title: WSL local gateway onboarding validation blockers from PR #274
source_issues.evidence: Validation harness reached PairOperator and failed with 'operator_auth_failed: Gateway rejected operator authentication'. Eight distinct blocking issues documented: (1) validation isolation writes to real user settings instead of isolated run folder, contaminating credentials; (2) validation launches stale tray executable from wrong output path; (3) operator pairing fails after gateway start with auth rejection; (4) token redaction gaps allow gateway tokens to leak into logs/UI diagnostics; (5) wsl.conf probe not section-aware and can pass/fail incorrectly; (6) docs describe [time] useWindowsTimezone but configurator does not write it; (7) cancellation leaves in-flight WSL commands running; (8) legacy DeviceToken vs NodeDeviceToken causes node startup to misread readiness.

signals.topic: Tray menu renders squished after Windows display DPI/scaling change until dismissed and reopened
signals.summary: When Windows display scaling is changed while the tray app is running, the right-click context menu renders squished/compressed on its first open at the new DPI scale. User must dismiss and reopen to get correct rendering.
signals.review_reason: Core UI element (tray context menu) renders incorrectly on DPI change — a common, expected Windows interaction. Requires dismiss-and-reopen workaround, creating noticeable UX degradation for any user who changes display scaling while the app is running.

source_issues.title: Tray menu flyout renders squished after display scaling change until dismissed and reopened
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on Windows 11 ARM64 at 100%, 125%, 150%, 200% scaling. Root cause: TrayMenuWindow is created once at startup and reused; SizeToContent() calls MenuPanel.Measure() which returns stale layout values from previous DPI because XAML layout pass hasn't re-rendered at new scale yet. Second open corrects itself after internal layout update.

signals.topic: Chat textbox does not auto-focus when chat window opens, requiring extra click
signals.summary: When the chat window is opened via tray icon left-click or right-click context menu, the chat textbox does not automatically receive keyboard focus. Users must click into the textbox before they can type.
signals.review_reason: Simple but definite UX friction on a core user-facing interaction (opening chat). Requires an extra unnecessary click every time the chat window opens, degrading the experience of the primary messaging surface.

source_issues.title: Chat textbox should auto-focus when window opens
source_issues.evidence: ShowNearTray() in ChatWindow.xaml.cs calls SetForegroundWindow to bring the window to foreground but does not call Focus() on the chat input element. Repro: open chat window and try typing immediately — nothing happens until user clicks the textbox.

signals.topic: Repo Assist automated workflow CI failure — copilot engine terminates with missing module error
signals.summary: The Repo Assist automated workflow (copilot engine) fails during CI runs with error: Cannot find module '/home/runner/work/_temp/gh-aw/actions/copilot_driver.cjs'. This prevents automated AI-assisted maintenance tasks from completing.
signals.review_reason: Automated workflow failure blocks AI-assisted maintenance (PR creation, security fixes, dependency updates) from running. While not a direct end-user product issue, it prevents the repo from receiving automated PR contributions, security bumps, and other maintenance that maintainers rely on.

source_issues.title: [aw] Repo Assist failed
source_issues.evidence: Workflow run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/25377223490 failed with 'Engine Failure: The copilot engine terminated before producing output' and error 'Cannot find module /home/runner/work/_temp/gh-aw/actions/copilot_driver.cjs'. Workflow generates automated issues and PRs for the repo.

signals.topic: Onboarding white/light cards render with unreadable white text in Windows dark mode
signals.summary: White and light-colored onboarding card surfaces (permissions page, connection page, ready page, wizard steps) do not set explicit foreground colors. In dark mode, the system theme's white text bleeds through against white backgrounds, making card text unreadable. Affects multiple onboarding pages beyond the yellow cards fixed in PR #257.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation during onboarding for dark mode users — text becomes unreadable on white card surfaces. Non-blocking since onboarding can still complete, but creates poor first impression and accessibility concern. Count=1 single-repository, non-blocking flow — P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Onboarding: white/light cards render unreadable text in dark mode (PR 241 follow-up)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause is same as PR #257 yellow card fix: hard-coded light backgrounds (#FFFFFF, #E8F4FD) with no explicit foreground, so dark mode white text bleeds through. Lists 6+ affected surfaces: OnboardingCard.cs, WizardStepView.cs, PermissionsPage.cs, ConnectionPage.cs, ReadyPage.cs, WizardPage.cs. All use .Background('#FFFFFF') without foreground. Visual verification requires screenshot capture via OPENCLAW_VISUAL_TEST=1.

signals.topic: Telegram message delays 3-6 minutes after upgrading to 2026.5.3+ (regression)
signals.summary: Telegram users experience 3-6 minute delays between sending messages and agent responding after upgrading from 2026.04.23 to 05.03/05.04. Gateway receives messages instantly but agent only activates minutes later.
signals.review_reason: 核心对话体验严重退化（从秒级变为分钟级），影响 Telegram 用户的主流程可用性。明确标记为 regression，有版本对比证据（2026.04.23 正常，2026.05.03+ 退化），且非 openclaw control page 复现表明是 Telegram 通道特有 regression。count=1 虽低于 P0 阈值，但因是 regression 且影响主流程交互，标记为 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: There is a 3–6-minute delay after sending telegram messages.
source_issues.evidence: Regression in 2026.05.03/05.04. User upgraded from 2026.04.23 and agent response went from seconds to 3-6 minutes. Gateway receives message instantly (verified in logs) but agent 'kicks in' only minutes later. Not reproduced on OpenClaw control page — Telegram-specific. Disabling active memory had no effect. Labels: bug + regression.

signals.topic: Zip file attachments blocked via message tool — regression from 2026.5.2
signals.summary: After upgrading from 2026.4.23 to 2026.5.2, sending .zip files as attachments via message tool fails with an allowlist error, blocking file transfer workflows that previously worked.
aliases: message tool file type allowlist regression
signals.review_reason: 明确 regression（2026.4.23 正常，2026.5.2 阻断），阻断文件传输核心工作流，用户需要传输 zip 源码文件但被拒绝。严重性高：影响 Discord 文件传输功能，agents 被迫使用不合适的 base64 编码 workaround。count=1 低于 P0，但 regression + 核心工作流阻断 + 清晰的用户影响证据，标记为 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Zip file attachments are blocked via the message tool
source_issues.evidence: Regression introduced in 2026.5.2. Before: worked dozens of times with 2026.4.23. After: error 'Host-local media sends only allow buffer-verified images, audio, video, PDF, and Office documents (got application/zip)'. Blocks users who need to transfer zipped source files. Agents try base64 encoding workaround which is inadequate.

signals.topic: macOS launchd-managed Gateway cannot access TCC-protected folders via CLI tools
signals.summary: When OpenClaw Gateway runs under macOS launchd, child CLI tools cannot access TCC-protected folders (~/Documents, ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop, Obsidian vaults) even when node has Full Disk Access. Same commands work from Terminal.app.
signals.review_reason: macOS 用户核心文件/CLI 工作流被阻断（Documents/Downloads/Obsidian 等受保护文件夹），仅影响 launchd 启动方式，正常终端启动正常。严重影响文件管理代理场景，workaround 需切换启动方式。count=1 低于 P0，但用户影响明确（permission denied on 常见操作），标记为 P1 合理。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: macOS launchd-managed Gateway cannot reliably access TCC-protected folders via CLI tools
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed PermissionError accessing ~/Documents/Obsidian Vault, obsidian-cli failures. Same gateway command works from Terminal.app. Root cause: launchd → node → openclaw gateway changes how child tools resolve TCC permissions. Affects any macOS user using local CLI tools for file operations or third-party integrations (Obsidian, etc.).

signals.topic: Discord multi-account: specialist bot commands hijack orchestrator routing causing 'channel not allowed' errors
signals.summary: In Discord multi-account setups, disabling native commands on specialist accounts (commands.native=false) does not remove stale global commands registered on Discord's side. This causes /side to route to specialist bots instead of the main orchestrator, returning 'This channel is not allowed' errors and preventing the main agent from seeing requests.
signals.review_reason: Discord 多账户配置下核心编排命令路由失败，主 agent 无法接收请求，用户看到误导性错误信息。根因是禁用原生命令后未清理 Discord 侧注册，手动 cleanup Discord API 是唯一 workaround。影响多账户部署场景。count=1，标记 P1。

source_issues.title: Discord per-account native command disable leaves stale specialist commands that can hijack /side

Environment: OpenClaw 2026.5.4, multi-account Discord with groupPolicy: allowlist.

signals.topic: Discord guild text slash commands silently dropped in preflight without user feedback
signals.summary: Discord guild-channel messages that look like slash commands (e.g., /steer ...) are silently dropped by the gateway's preflight handler before reaching the agent session. Users receive no error or feedback — the message simply vanishes.
aliases: Discord text slash command silent drop
signals.review_reason: 消息静默丢失无任何反馈是严重的 UX 问题，用户无法判断命令是否被接收，导致反复重试或遗漏。根因是 preflight 层 early return null，未走正常授权/错误路径。明确阻断用户交互。count=1，标记 P1。

source_issues.title: Discord guild text slash commands are silently dropped before agent session
source_issues.evidence: User sent /steer ... as plain text in a Discord project channel. Discord did not execute it as a native slash command (wrong message type), OpenClaw intercepted it and returned null at gateway preflight. Agent never saw it and no rejection/usage message was sent. User only got attention after sending a plain-text follow-up. Root cause: message-handler.preflight has early return null for hasControlCommand() matches in guild text messages.

signals.topic: pip/uvx installation fails on Python 3.13+ due to PyO3 compatibility with tiktoken dependency
signals.summary: open-interpreter cannot be installed via pip or uvx on Python 3.13+ because its tiktoken dependency uses PyO3 v0.20.3 which caps Python support at 3.12. This completely blocks the main installation flow across Windows 11 and macOS.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct users across Windows 11 and macOS are completely blocked from installing open-interpreter via pip/uvx due to tiktoken's PyO3 dependency not supporting Python 3.13+. This is a main-flow failure: users cannot even run the tool. The root cause is consistent (PyO3 v0.20.3 caps at Python 3.12), reproducible across platforms, and explicitly prevents installation. Confidence is high as all 3 issues have identical error patterns and user-impact evidence.

signals.topic: Arbitrary file read vulnerability in image_documents_to_base64 via user-supplied ImageDocument metadata
signals.summary: image_documents_to_base64 opens any path in ImageDocument.metadata['file_path'] without allowlisting, symlink checks, or MIME validation, exposing arbitrary file read to any multimodal LLM when paths come from user data (tool args, JSON bodies).
aliases: Arbitrary file read via ImageDocument file_path
signals.review_reason: Security vulnerability with clear exploitation path: any application building ImageDocument from user-supplied paths (common in agent/tool workflows) exposes arbitrary file read whose output is sent to the LLM. This is not theoretical — the code pattern is directly in a public utility function.

source_issues.title: Arbitrary file read via ImageDocument.metadata["file_path"] in image_documents_to_base64

signals.topic: IngestionPipeline with num_workers > 1 silently drops all cache writes, causing expensive re-execution including re-embedding
signals.summary: In multi-worker pipeline runs, cache entries written by workers are lost because only transformed nodes are returned to the parent process. Each worker mutates its own in-memory copy, and those writes vanish on worker exit. pipeline.persist() also excludes these entries.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost loss: every multi-worker run loses all cache entries including expensive embedding operations, forcing full re-execution each time. The failure is completely silent with no error raised, so users may not realize their caching is broken.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: IngestionPipeline with `num_workers > 1` silently loses all cache writes
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: self.cache is passed to workers which write entries there, but only transformed nodes are returned. With SimpleKVStore each worker mutates its own in-memory copy lost on exit. Subsequent runs re-execute expensive transforms including embeddings. pipeline.persist() also misses these entries.

signals.review_reason: Complete feature blockage: the vLLM integration throws a TypeError on every call with current vLLM versions (>=0.19.0), making it entirely unusable. This is a breaking regression for any user trying to use local vLLM models.

signals.topic: Bash hook creates empty files at project root via shell injection through $TOOL_INPUT_command interpolation
signals.summary: hooks.json interpolates $TOOL_INPUT_command into a double-quoted string. When bash commands contain double quotes (node -e "...", python -c "...", git commit -m "..."), the wrapping quotes break and shell re-parses inner content. Any > character is interpreted as redirection, silently creating empty files at project root. After ~24h of normal usage, dozens of empty files accumulate (names like 3, maxWidth), console.log(k)), etc.) with no error logged.
signals.review_reason: P0: Data pollution affecting every Windows project using claude-flow plugin. Silent accumulation of empty files at project root with names derived from code content after > characters. Causes corrupted working directory state with no error indication.
